records.name: abiyuch
records.description: Abiyuch comes from Crateva religiosa, commonly known as the sacred garlic pear or temple plant. It's a species of flowering tree that belongs to the caper family.

records.name: Abondance
records.description: Abondance is a semi-hard, fragrant, raw-milk cheese made in the Haute-Savoie department of France.

records.name: absinthe
records.description: ABSINTHE is historically described as a distilled, highly alcoholic beverage

records.name: added sugar
records.description: Added sugar is an ingredient that describes anything that counts as sugar.

records.name: agathi leaves
records.description: Agathi leaves (Sesbania grandiflora) originate from South and Southeast Asia, where the tree grows widely across tropical and subtropical regions. The leaves have a mildly bitter, slightly grassy taste that softens when cooked. Culinarily, they're used in soups, stir-fries, lentil dishes, and traditional preparations across Indian, Sri Lankan, Thai, and Filipino cuisines, often paired with tamarind, coconut, or spices. Nutritionally, agathi leaves are notable for their high vitamin A, vitamin C, calcium, and iron content, along with protein and dietary fiber. They also contain antioxidants and various phytonutrients, making them a traditionally valued leafy green in many regional food cultures worldwide.

records.name: agave syrup
records.description: Agave syrup (or agave nectar) is a liquid sweetener extracted from the core of the agave plant, particularly Agave tequilana, with production centered in Mexico where the plant has long been used to make traditional sweeteners and beverages like pulque. It has a mild, neutral sweetness—often noted as sweeter than honey—with subtle caramel notes in darker varieties, and a thin, smooth, honey-like texture that dissolves easily in cold liquids. Popular as a vegan honey substitute in beverages, baking, and dressings, agave syrup is very high in fructose (often 70-90%), giving it a low glycemic index despite being calorie-dense, though its fructose concentration has raised similar metabolic concerns as high-fructose corn syrup.

records.name: alaska pollock
records.description: The Alaska pollock (Gadus chalcogrammus) is a marine fish species of the cod family Gadidae.

records.name: albacore
records.description: The albacore (Thunnus alalunga), known also as the longfin tuna, is a species of tuna of the order Perciformes.

records.name: Alkaline noodles
records.description: variation of noodles with a much higher quantity of alkali than usual. The most common examples are Chinese Lamian noodles and Japanese Ramen noodles.

records.name: allspice
records.description: ALLSPICE, also known as Jamaica pepper, myrtle pepper, pimenta, or pimento, is the dried unripe berry of Pimenta dioica, a midcanopy tree native to the Greater Antilles, southern Mexico, and Central America, now cultivated in many warm parts of the world.

records.name: almond
records.description: The almond (Prunus amygdalus, syn. Prunus dulcis) is a species of tree native to Iran and surrounding countries, but widely cultivated elsewhere. The almond is also the name of the edible and widely cultivated seed of this tree.

records.name: aloe vera
records.description: ALOE VERA is a succulent plant species of the genus Aloe.

records.name: amaranth
records.description: Amaranth is an ancient pseudocereal native to Central and South America, prized by the Aztecs as a staple crop alongside corn and beans. It has an earthy, slightly peppery flavor with a distinctive sticky, porridge-like texture when cooked, and it pops like tiny popcorn when toasted dry in a hot pan. Naturally gluten-free, amaranth stands out for its unusually high protein content complete with lysine (an amino acid most grains lack), along with good levels of iron, magnesium, and calcium.

records.name: amaretto
records.description: Amaretto (Italian for "a little bitter") is a sweet Italian liqueur that originated in Saronno, Italy.

records.name: American butterfish
records.description: American butterfish (Peprilus triacanthus) is a small, deep-bodied fish from the northwest Atlantic, ranging from Labrador down to Florida's Gulf coast. Flavor and texture: It has soft, delicate, oily flesh with a mild, sweet flavor — the "butter" in the name comes from that rich, tender texture rather than any actual buttery taste. The flesh is white and flakes easily when cooked.

records.name: american cranberry
records.description: Vaccinium macrocarpon (also called large cranberry, American cranberry and bearberry) is a North American species of cranberry of the subgenus Oxycoccus and genus Vaccinium.

records.name: American sea scallop
records.description: Placopecten magellanicus, common names Atlantic deep-sea scallop, deep sea scallop, North Atlantic sea scallop, American sea scallop, Atlantic sea scallop, or sea scallop, is a commercially important pectinid bivalve mollusk native to the northwest Atlantic Ocean.

records.name: ancho peppers
records.description: Ancho peppers are the dried form of the poblano pepper. Sweet and fruity with notes of raisin, dried plum, and a mild smokiness — sometimes with a hint of coffee or tobacco. It's considered one of the more complex, dessert-like tasting dried chiles.

records.name: animal fat
records.description: ANIMAL FATS and oils are lipid materials derived from animals. Physically, oils are liquid at room temperature, and fats are solid. Although many animal parts and secretions may yield oil, in commercial practice, oil is extracted primarily from rendered tissue fats obtained from livestock animals like pigs, chickens and cows.

records.name: animal-based rennet
records.description: CALF RENNET is extracted from the inner mucosa of the fourth stomach chamber (the abomasum) of young, unweaned calves as part of livestock butchering.

records.name: aniseed
records.description: Anise, also called aniseed, is a flowering plant in the family Apiaceae. It is widely cultivated and used to flavor food and alcoholic drinks, especially around the Mediterranean.

records.name: aniseed oil
records.description: ANISEED OIL is an essential oil, which is obtained by steam distillation from the crushed fruits of the anise (Pimpinella anisum) and the real star anise (Illicium verum)

records.name: apple cider vinegar
records.description: CIDER VINEGAR, a vinegar made from apples, sugar and yeast

records.name: apple juice
aliases: apple juice made from fresh apples

records.name: apricot
records.description: Apricots are stone fruits believed to have originated in China or Central Asia thousands of years ago, later spreading along the Silk Road through Persia and into the Mediterranean, where regions like Turkey and California became major modern producers. They have a delicate, sweet-tart flavor with subtle floral and honeyed notes, and a soft, velvety-skinned flesh that's juicy when ripe and firms into a chewy, concentrated sweetness when dried. Eaten fresh, dried, or used in jams, baking, and savory glazes, apricots are a good source of vitamin A (from beta-carotene), vitamin C, and fiber, with dried apricots also offering a notable concentration of iron and potassium.

records.name: apricot juice from concentrate and puree
aliases: apricot juice from concentrate and puree
apricot juice made from cremogenate and concentrate

records.name: arctic char
records.description: The Arctic char or Arctic charr (Salvelinus alpinus) is a cold-water fish in the family Salmonidae, native to alpine lakes and arctic and subarctic coastal waters. The flesh is fine-flaked and medium firm. The colour is between light pink and deep red, and the taste is like something between trout and salmon.

records.name: argan oil
records.description: argan oil is found in argan tree

records.name: arrowhead
records.description: Arrowhead (also called Sagittaria, water arrowhead, or 慈姑 cí gū in Chinese) is an aquatic plant whose starchy corms (bulb-like root tubers) are eaten as a vegetable. It grows in shallow ponds, marshes, and rice paddies, and is especially popular in Chinese, Japanese, and Southeast Asian cooking. Mildly bitter and slightly sweet, with a starchy texture similar to a chestnut or potato. The bitterness mellows considerably with cooking.

records.name: arrowroot
records.description: Arrowroot (Maranta arundinacea) is a tropical plant native to the Caribbean and Central/South America. It's a rhizome — an underground stem, similar in concept to ginger or turmeric. Arrowroot is most famous as a starch/thickener rather than a table vegetable.

records.name: arrowroot powder
records.description: Arrowroot starch is a starch obtained from the rhizomes (rootstock) of several tropical plants, traditionally Maranta arundinacea, but also Florida arrowroot from Zamia integrifolia, and tapioca from cassava (Manihot esculenta), which is often labelled as arrowroot.

records.name: Arrowtooth flounder
records.description: The arrowtooth flounder (Atheresthes stomas) is a fish in the family Pleuronectidae.

records.name: artichoke
records.description: The globe ARTICHOKE (Cynara cardunculus var. scolymus), also known as French artichoke and green artichoke in the USA, is a variety of a species of thistle cultivated as a food. Leaves are often removed one at a time, and the fleshy base eaten, with hollandaise, vinegar, butter, mayonnaise, aioli, lemon juice, or other sauces. The fibrous upper part of each leaf is usually discarded. The heart is eaten when the inedible choke has been peeled away from the base and discarded. The thin leaves covering the choke are also edible.

records.name: Artichoke heart
records.description: The heart is eaten when the inedible choke has been peeled away from the base and discarded.

records.name: asafoetida
records.description: A resinous gum from the stem and roots of Ferula species such as Ferula foetida and Ferula assa-foetida, having a strong, unpleasant smell, with culinary and medical uses

records.name: Ashitaba
records.description: species of flowering plant in the carrot family

records.name: Asiago
records.description: Asiago is an Italian cow's milk cheese that can assume different textures, according to its aging, from smooth for the fresh Asiago to a crumbly texture for the aged cheese.

records.name: asparagus
records.description: Asparagus, or garden asparagus, folk name sparrow grass, scientific name Asparagus officinalis is a spring vegetable, a flowering perennial plant species in the genus Asparagus;

records.name: atlantic salmon
records.description: The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.

records.name: Atlantic wolffish
records.description: The Atlantic wolffish (Anarhichas lupus), also known as the seawolf, Atlantic catfish, ocean catfish, devil fish, wolf eel (the common name for its Pacific relative), woof or sea cat, is a marine fish of the wolffish family Anarhichadidae.

records.name: atta
records.description: Atta is whole wheat flour, stone-ground or milled from Triticum aestivum using the entire grain — bran, germ, and endosperm intact. This traditional chakki-milling method has been used across South Asia for centuries, predating industrial refining. Atta has a warm, nutty, slightly earthy taste with a denser, coarser texture than refined flour. It's the staple for everyday Indian breads — roti, chapati, paratha — and is also used in some baked goods. Nutritionally, it's rich in fiber, iron, magnesium, and B-vitamins (retained from the bran and germ), with a lower glycemic index than maida, making it more filling and slower-digesting.

records.name: avocado
records.description: The AVOCADO (Persea americana) is a tree classified as a member of the flowering plant family Lauraceae. The fruit of the plant, also called an avocado, is botanically a large berry containing a single large seed.

records.name: babassu oil
records.description: Babassu oil is a light, natural vegetable oil extracted from the seeds of the babassu palm tree (Orbignya phalerata), native to the Amazon rainforest region of Brazil. It's also valued for its sustainability credentials, as harvesting supports traditional Amazonian communities (particularly women harvesters known as quebradeiras de coco).

records.name: Bacillus coagulans
records.description: BACILLUS COAGULANS is a lactic acid-forming bacterial species. B. coagulans is often marketed as Lactobacillus sporogenes or a 'sporeforming lactic acid bacterium' probiotic, but this is an outdated name due to taxonomic changes in 1939.

records.name: bacon
records.description: Bacon is a type of salt-cured pork. Bacon is prepared from several different cuts of meat, typically from the pork belly or from back cuts, which have less fat than the belly. It is eaten on its own, as a side dish (particularly in breakfasts), or used as a minor ingredient to flavour dishes

records.name: baker's yeast
records.description: Baker's yeast is the common name for active Saccharomyces cerevisiae used specifically for baking, cultivated commercially since the late 19th century when compressed yeast production made it widely accessible, replacing older methods like sourdough starters and brewer's yeast. It has a mild, slightly savory flavor with little aroma on its own, though it develops the characteristic yeasty, bready aroma during fermentation, and is sold as fresh (compressed), active dry, or instant granules. Used to leaven bread, rolls, and pastries, baker's yeast works by converting sugars into carbon dioxide and alcohol, and while used in small quantities, it contributes trace amounts of B vitamins and protein alongside its primary leavening function.

records.name: balsamic vinegar
records.description: Balsamic vinegar is a very dark, concentrated, and intensely flavoured vinegar originating in Italy, made wholly or partially from grape must, grape juice with all the skins, seeds and stems.

records.name: bamboo
records.description: The bamboos are evergreen perennial flowering plants in the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.

records.name: bamboo shoot
records.description: Bamboo shoots or bamboo sprouts are the edible shoots (new bamboo culms that come out of the ground) of many bamboo species including Bambusa vulgaris and Phyllostachys edulis.

records.name: banana
records.description: Bananas are tropical fruits believed to have originated in Southeast Asia and Papua New Guinea thousands of years ago, later spreading through Africa and eventually the Americas, where they became one of the world's most widely consumed and traded fruits. They have a sweet, mild, slightly tangy flavor with a soft, creamy texture that ripens from starchy and firm to soft and sugary as the fruit matures. Eaten fresh, cooked, or dried, and used in baking, smoothies, and desserts, bananas are notably rich in potassium, vitamin B6, and fiber, along with natural sugars that make them a popular quick energy source.

records.name: banana pepper
records.description: Banana peppers are a mild, tangy pepper named for their curved, elongated shape and pale yellow color — closely resembling a banana. Tangy and slightly sweet with a mild vinegary bite, especially when pickled — very different from the "grassy" heat of a jalapeño.

records.name: barley
records.description: barley (hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally

records.name: barley flour
records.description: Barley flour or meal is made by grinding whole or pearled barley grains into a fine (flour) or coarse (meal) powder. Good source of dietary fiber, especially beta-glucan (a soluble fiber linked to cholesterol and blood sugar benefits), provides B vitamins, selenium, and manganese.

records.name: basella leaves
records.description: Basella alba, commonly called Malabar spinach or vine spinach, is a fast-growing climbing vine native to tropical Asia and Africa, now cultivated widely across South and Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean. Its thick, glossy leaves have a mild, slightly peppery taste and a mucilaginous texture similar to okra when cooked. Popular in stir-fries, soups, curries, and stews, it holds up well in hot, humid climates where true spinach struggles. Nutritionally, the leaves are rich in vitamins A and C, iron, calcium, and antioxidants, with a naturally high water and fiber content, making them a staple leafy green in many traditional cuisines worldwide.

records.name: basmati rice
records.description: BASMATI RICE is a variety of long, slender-grained aromatic rice which is traditionally from the Indian subcontinent.

records.name: bastardo
records.description: Trousseau or Trousseau Noir, also known as Bastardo, is an old variety of red wine grape originating in eastern France.

records.name: bathua leaves
records.description: Bathua, also known as fat hen or lamb's quarters, is a wild leafy green native to Europe and Asia, now naturalized worldwide and especially prized in North Indian cuisine during winter months. Its leaves have an earthy, slightly tangy, spinach-like flavor with a tender texture when cooked. Traditionally used in soups, flatbreads (bathua paratha), raita, and sautéed side dishes, it's often paired with lentils or mustard greens. Nutritionally, bathua is notable for its iron, calcium, vitamin A, vitamin C, and protein content, along with dietary fiber, making it a valued seasonal green across many traditional food cultures globally.

records.name: beans
records.description: A BEAN is a seed of one of several genera of the flowering plant family Fabaceae, which are used for human or animal food.

records.name: béarnaise sauce
records.description: BÉARNAISE SAUCE is a sauce made of clarified butter emulsified in egg yolks and white wine vinegar and flavored with herbs.

records.name: Beaufort
records.description: Beaufort is a firm, raw cow's milk cheese associated with the gruyère family.

records.name: beechnut
records.description: Beechnuts are the small, triangular nuts produced by beech trees (genus Fagus), particularly the American beech (Fagus grandifolia) and European beech (Fagus sylvatica). They're edible for humans in moderate amounts, but raw beechnuts contain a compound called fagin (sometimes also referenced as related tannins) that can cause mild digestive upset or headaches if eaten in large quantities. Roasting them reduces this and improves flavor.

records.name: beet greens
records.description: Beet greens are the leafy tops of the beetroot plant (Beta vulgaris), native to the Mediterranean and Near East, where wild sea beet has been used since antiquity. They have an earthy, slightly bitter flavor with mild sweetness, similar to Swiss chard, and tender-crisp stems ranging from white to deep red. Widely used across Mediterranean, European, Middle Eastern, and South Asian cuisines, they are sautéed, steamed, added to soups, stews, and stir-fries, or eaten raw in salads when young. Nutritionally, beet greens are rich in vitamins A, C, and K, along with folate, potassium, magnesium, iron, and dietary fiber, plus antioxidant compounds including betalains.

records.name: beetroot
records.description: BEETROOT is the taproot portion of the beet plant

records.name: bell pepper
records.description: The bell pepper (also known as sweet pepper, pepper or capsicum /ˈkæpsɪkəm/) is a cultivar group of the species Capsicum annuum. Cultivars of the plant produce fruits in different colours, including red, yellow, orange, green, white, and purple.

records.name: berries
records.description: Berries are small, fleshy, typically sweet-tart fruits produced by a wide range of flowering plants, growing wild across temperate and cold regions worldwide long before cultivation, with varieties like strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries becoming widely farmed staples in Europe and North America. They have a flavor ranging from intensely sweet to sharply tart, often balanced with floral or earthy notes, and a soft, juicy texture that varies from the delicate burst of raspberries to the firmer bite of blueberries. Eaten fresh, dried, or used in jams, baking, and beverages, berries are notably rich in antioxidants (especially anthocyanins), fiber, and vitamin C, making them among the most nutrient-dense fruits.

records.name: beta-galactosidase
records.description: Β-GALACTOSIDASE is a glycoside hydrolase enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of β-galactosides into monosaccharides through the breaking of a glycosidic bond. β-galactosidase is important for the lactose intolerant community as it is responsible for making lactose-free milk and other dairy products. Many adult humans lack the lactase enzyme, which has the same function of beta-gal, so they are not able to properly digest dairy products. Beta-galactose is used in such dairy products as yogurt, sour cream, and some cheeses which are treated with the enzyme to break down any lactose before human consumption.

records.name: betel leaves
records.description: Betel leaf (Piper betle) is a heart-shaped, glossy leaf native to Southeast Asia, now cultivated across South and Southeast Asia and parts of the Pacific. It has a pungent, peppery, slightly bitter flavor with an aromatic, faintly numbing quality from natural essential oils. Globally, it's best known as the wrapper for paan, but is also used to wrap savory bites (as in Thai miang kham), chopped into chutneys, or used to wrap fish before steaming. Nutritionally, the leaf contains vitamins A and C, calcium, and trace minerals, along with aromatic compounds like eugenol and chavicol that contribute to its distinctive taste and traditional uses.

records.name: Bifidobacterium bifidum
records.description: BIFIDOBACTERIUM BIFIDUM is a bacterial species of the genus Bifidobacterium. B. bifidum is one of the most common probiotic bacteria that can be found in the body of mammals, including humans.

records.name: Bifidobacterium lactis
records.description: BIFIDOBACTERIUM ANIMALIS is a gram-positive, anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium of the Bifidobacterium genus which can be found in the large intestines of humans. Both old names B. animalis and B. lactis are still used on product labels, as this species is frequently used as a probiotic. In most cases, which subspecies is used in the product is not clear. Several companies have attempted to trademark particular strains, and as a marketing technique, have invented scientific-sounding names for the strains.

records.name: Bifidobacterium longum
records.description: BIFIDOBACTERIUM LONGUM is a Gram-positive, catalase-negative, rod-shaped bacterium present in the human gastrointestinal tract. B. longum is non-pathogenic and is often added to food products.

records.name: bifidus
records.description: BIFIDOBACTERIUM is a genus of gram-positive, nonmotile, often branched anaerobic bacteria. They are ubiquitous inhabitants of the gastrointestinal tract, vagina and mouth of mammals humans.

records.name: bifidus actiregularis
records.description: Danone decided to add a probiotic strain: BIFIDUS ACTIREGULARIS. Activia products thus contain Bifidobacterium animalis DN 173,010, a proprietary strain of Bifidobacterium, a probiotic which is marketed by Dannon under the trade names Bifidus Regularis, Bifidus Actiregularis, Bifidus Digestivum and Bifidobacterium Lactis.

records.name: biscuit
records.description: A BISCUIT is a flour-based baked food product, which is typically hard, flat and unleavened.

records.name: bitter melon
records.description: A balsam pear is another name for bitter melon (Momordica charantia), a tropical vine in the gourd family. It's widely grown across Asia, Africa, the Caribbean, and South America. True to both its names, it has a pronounced bitter taste — the most bitter of any commonly eaten vegetable.

records.name: black amaranth seed
records.description: Native to Central and South America, amaranth was a staple grain of the Aztec and Inca civilizations, prized for its resilience and nutritional density. Black amaranth seeds have a mild, earthy, slightly peppery flavor with a subtle nuttiness that intensifies when toasted or popped. Versatile in the kitchen, they can be cooked like porridge, popped for snacking or garnishing, ground into flour for gluten-free baking, or sprouted for salads and bowls. Nutritionally, amaranth is a complete protein containing all nine essential amino acids, including lysine—rare among grains. It's also rich in fiber, iron, magnesium, and manganese, and naturally gluten-free, making it a nutrient-dense choice for ancient-grain and health-focused products.

records.name: black kidney bean
records.description: Black Rajmah (black kidney beans) originates from the Andean region of Central and South America, later becoming a staple across South Asia, particularly in North Indian and Kashmiri cuisine. Distinct from the more common red rajmah, it has a deep black-maroon skin and a dense, creamy interior with an earthy, slightly sweet flavor. It's typically slow-cooked in a thick, spiced tomato-onion gravy, served with rice or flatbread, and also used in stews, salads, and bean-based dishes worldwide. Nutritionally, it's rich in plant protein, dietary fiber, complex carbohydrates, iron, folate, and antioxidants, making it a valued legume across many global culinary traditions.

records.name: black seabream
records.description: The black seabream (Spondyliosoma cantharus) is a species of Sparidae fishes. They live in northern Europe and in the Mediterranean.

records.name: black soy bean
records.description: Black soybeans (Glycine max) are a dark-seed-coated variety of soybean cultivated across East Asia, including China, Korea, and Japan, with production also found in parts of North America and elsewhere. Their flavor is earthier and nuttier than yellow soybeans, with a subtle sweetness when cooked. Traditionally used in braised side dishes, black bean pastes, teas, fermented condiments, and specialty tofu, they hold cultural significance in many Asian culinary traditions. Nutritionally, they are rich in plant protein and dietary fiber, and their black seed coat contains anthocyanins, the same antioxidant pigments found in blueberries and black rice.

records.name: Blend of EU and non-EU honeys
aliases: blend of eu and non eu honeys

records.name: bleu d'auvergne
records.description: Bleu d'Auvergne is a French AOP blue cheese, made from cow's milk, named for its place of origin in the Auvergne region of south-central France.

records.name: bleu de Bresse
records.description: Bleu de Bresse is a blue cheese made from whole milk.

records.name: bleu de gex
records.description: Bleu de Gex (also Bleu du Haut-Jura or Bleu de Septmoncel) is a creamy, semi-soft blue cheese made from unpasteurized milk in the Jura region of France.

records.name: blue cheese
records.description: Blue cheese or bleu cheese is cheese made with cultures of the mold Penicillium, giving it spots or veins of the mold throughout the cheese, which can vary in color through various shades of blue and green.

records.name: blue ling
records.description: Blue ling lives in much deeper water than common ling. The flesh is white, firm, and mild — used in much the same way as common ling or cod, though it's less commonly sold fresh to consumers and more often ends up in processed or filleted products.

records.name: blue whiting
records.description: The blue whiting, Micromesistius poutassou, one of the two species in the genus Micromesistius in the cod family, is common in the northeast Atlantic Ocean from Morocco to Iceland and Spitsbergen

records.name: bluefish
records.description: Bluefish (Pomatomus saltatrix) is a species of saltwater fish commonly eaten as food, especially along the Atlantic coasts of the US, and also found in various other parts of the world. Flavor and texture: It has a stronger, more "fishy" flavor than mild white fish like cod or tilapia. The flesh is oily/fatty (similar in that regard to mackerel or salmon), which gives it a rich taste but also means it spoils faster and is best cooked fresh.

records.name: boiled egg
records.description: Boiled eggs are eggs, typically from a chicken, cooked with their shells unbroken, usually by immersion in boiling water.

records.name: bolognese sauce
records.description: BOLOGNESE SAUCE is a meat-based sauce in Italian cuisine. It is customarily used to dress tagliatelle al ragù and to prepare lasagne alla bolognese.

records.name: borage
records.description: Borage, also known as a starflower, is an annual herb in the flowering plant family Boraginaceae. It is native to the Mediterranean region. Borage is used as either a fresh vegetable or a dried herb.

records.name: borlotti bean
records.description: The borlotti bean is a variety of common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) first bred in Colombia as the cargamanto.

records.name: boston butt
records.description: BOSTON BUTT, or pork butt, is the American name for a cut of pork that comes from the upper part of the shoulder from the front leg and may contain the blade bone.  Boston butt is the most common cut used for pulled pork, a staple of barbecue in the southern United States.

records.name: brandy
records.description: BRANDY is a spirit produced by distilling wine. Brandy generally contains 35–60% alcohol by volume (70–120 US proof) and is typically consumed as an after-dinner digestif.

records.name: brazil nut
records.description: The Brazil nut (Bertholletia excelsa) is a South American tree in the family Lecythidaceae, and it is also the name of the tree's commercially harvested edible seeds.

records.name: breadfruit
records.description: Breadfruit is a starchy tropical fruit native to the South Pacific and Southeast Asia, long cultivated across Polynesian islands as a dietary staple, and historically significant for its role in the 18th-century Bounty voyage, which aimed to transplant it to the Caribbean as cheap food for enslaved laborers. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor reminiscent of fresh bread or potato when cooked, with a starchy, dense texture similar to a potato when roasted, boiled, or fried. Typically eaten cooked rather than raw, breadfruit is a good source of complex carbohydrates, fiber, potassium, and vitamin C, making it a nutrient-dense staple food in many tropical regions.

records.name: breadnut tree seeds
records.description: Breadnut (also called kamansi in the Philippines, or "chataigne" in the Caribbean) produces large, spiky green fruits similar in appearance to breadfruit, but unlike the common seedless breadfruit variety, breadnut fruits are packed with edible seeds — usually 100+ per fruit. The seeds themselves are roughly the size of chestnuts or large beans. Typically boiled, roasted, or steamed before eating. After cooking, the texture is starchy and nutty, often compared to chestnuts or roasted potatoes.

records.name: brewer's yeast
records.description: SACCHAROMYCES CEREVISIAE is a species of yeast. It has been instrumental to winemaking, baking, and brewing since ancient times. S. cerevisiae is used in baking; the carbon dioxide generated by the fermentation is used as a leavening agent in bread and other baked goods. Historically, this use was closely linked to the brewing industry's use of yeast, as bakers took or bought the barm or yeast-filled foam from brewing ale from the brewers (producing the barm cake); today, brewing and baking yeast strains are somewhat different.

records.name: Brewing water
records.description: Brewing water is water specifically treated or selected for beer or coffee production, with mineral content—calcium, magnesium, sulfate, chloride, and bicarbonate—carefully adjusted to match regional styles, a practice tracing back to historic brewing centers like Burton-on-Trent (high sulfate, favoring hoppy pale ales) and Pilsen (very soft water, ideal for delicate lagers). It has a neutral base flavor, but its mineral balance subtly shapes the final beverage's taste—sulfate accentuates hop bitterness and dryness, while chloride enhances malt sweetness and mouthfeel. Used as the primary ingredient in brewing (making up roughly 90-95% of beer), water's mineral profile is often adjusted through filtration, dilution, or targeted mineral additions to achieve consistency and match desired beer or coffee styles. As with plain water, brewing water contains no calories, protein, fat, or carbohydrates, only trace minerals that influence flavor rather than nutrition.

records.name: Brie
records.description: Brie is a soft cow's-milk cheese named after Brie, the French region from which it originated. It is pale in color with a slight grayish tinge under a rind of white mould.

records.name: Brie de Meaux
aliases: brie de meaux cheese from cows milk
records.description: Brie de Meaux is an unpasteurized brie, manufactured in the town of Meaux in the Brie region of northern France since the 8th century.

records.name: Brie de Melun
aliases: brie de melun cheese from cows milk
records.description: Brie de Melun is a brie made with unpasteurized milk.

records.name: brioche
records.description: Brioche is a bread of French origin that is similar to a highly enriched pastry, and whose high egg and butter content give it a rich and tender crumb.

records.name: broad bean
records.description: Vicia faba, also known in the culinary sense as the broad bean, fava bean, or faba bean is a species of flowering plant in the pea and bean family Fabaceae.

records.name: broad-leaved endive
records.description: Escarole, or broad-leaved endive (var latifolia), has broad, pale green leaves and is less bitter than the other varieties. Varieties or names include Batavian endive, grumolo, scarola, and scarole.

records.name: broccoli raab
records.description: Broccoli raab (also spelled rabe, and sometimes called rapini) is a leafy green vegetable popular in Italian and Mediterranean cooking. Despite its name, it's not closely related to regular broccoli — it's actually more closely related to turnips. It has long, thin stalks with dark green, slightly jagged leaves and small florets that resemble tiny broccoli heads. The whole plant is edible — leaves, stems, and florets. Its defining characteristic is a pleasantly bitter, slightly pungent, nutty flavor, much more assertive than regular broccoli.

records.name: brown kidney bean
records.description: Brown Rajmah (brown kidney beans) traces its origins to the Andean highlands of the Americas, from where it spread globally and became widely cultivated across South Asia, especially in Kashmir and northern India. It has a light tan-brown skin with a mild, nutty, slightly earthy flavor and a firmer texture than red or black varieties. Commonly simmered in spiced curries, added to soups, stews, salads, and rice dishes, it's valued in cuisines worldwide for its versatility. Nutritionally, brown rajmah offers plant-based protein, dietary fiber, complex carbohydrates, iron, magnesium, and folate, making it a nourishing legume across diverse global food cultures.

records.name: brown soybean
records.description: Brown soybeans (Glycine max) are a tan-to-brown-seed-coated variety grown throughout East Asia, particularly in China, Japan, and Korea, alongside cultivation in other soybean-producing regions worldwide. Compared to common yellow soybeans, they offer a nuttier, slightly roasted, and subtly sweet flavor. They are traditionally used in specialty soy sauces, roasted soy snacks, and certain regional tofu preparations, valued for the distinct character their seed coat lends to fermented and cooked dishes. Nutritionally, brown soybeans provide a strong source of plant protein and dietary fiber, similar to other soybean varieties, with their color coming from natural pigments in the seed coat.

records.name: brown sugar
records.description: Brown sugar is sugar—typically from sugarcane—that retains or has molasses added back in during processing, a practice with roots in unrefined "raw" sugars historically produced across the Caribbean, South Asia, and other cane-growing regions before fully refined white sugar became standard. It has a rich, warm, caramel-like flavor with subtle toffee and mineral notes from the molasses, and a moist, clumping texture ranging from light to dark depending on molasses content. Commonly used in baking, glazes, and sauces for its depth and moisture, brown sugar offers only trace minerals like calcium and iron from the molasses, making it nutritionally almost identical to white sugar—still primarily empty calories.

records.name: brussels sprouts
records.description: Brussels sprouts are small, leafy green vegetables belonging to the cabbage family, believed to have originated in Belgium, from which they take their name, though similar plants trace back to ancient Rome. They grow in tight, bud-like clusters along a thick stalk. Raw, they have a slightly bitter, peppery bite; cooked, they turn nuttier and sweeter, especially when roasted, caramelized, or charred. Popular worldwide, they're prepared by roasting, steaming, sautéing, or shredding into slaws, often paired with garlic, bacon, nuts, or citrus. Nutritionally, they're rich in fiber, vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, and antioxidant compounds, while remaining low in calories.

records.name: buckwheat
records.description: Buckwheat, despite its name, isn't a wheat relative at all—it's a fruit seed related to rhubarb, originating in Central Asia and cultivated in China for thousands of years before spreading through Europe and Russia. Its groats have an earthy, nutty flavor with a slight bitterness that deepens when toasted (as in kasha), and they're used whole, ground into flour, or sprouted in dishes ranging from soba noodles to porridge and pancakes. Naturally gluten-free, buckwheat is a good source of plant protein, fiber, magnesium, and manganese, plus rutin, an antioxidant linked to cardiovascular benefits.

records.name: bulgur
records.description: Bulgur is a parboiled wheat product made by steaming or boiling whole wheat kernels, drying them, then cracking them into coarse or fine granules. Originating in the Middle East/Mediterranean region thousands of years ago (a staple in Levantine and Turkish cuisine), it retains the bran and germ since it's made from whole wheat. It has a mild, nutty, slightly toasty taste and a light, fluffy texture once rehydrated. Used in tabbouleh, pilafs, soups, and as a quick-cooking rice substitute. Nutritionally, it's high in fiber and protein, with more iron, magnesium, and B-vitamins retained than refined flour, and a moderate glycemic index.

records.name: bullocks heart
records.description: Native to the Caribbean and Central America, but now grown across tropical regions of South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Africa. The flesh inside is white to pale yellow, soft, and creamy, though generally considered less refined in flavor than its relatives

records.name: burbot
records.description: Burbot (Lota lota) is a freshwater fish — and actually the only member of the cod family (Gadidae) that lives entirely in fresh water rather than the ocean. It's edible and considered quite good eating — sometimes nicknamed "poor man's lobster" because its liver and flesh are prized by some anglers, especially for winter ice-fishing.

records.name: burdock root
records.description: Burdock root is an edible root vegetable and herbal remedy that comes from the burdock plant (Arctium lappa), a large-leafed plant native to northern Asia and Europe, now grown worldwide. it's especially popular in Japanese cuisine, where it's known as gobō. It has a mildly sweet, earthy flavor and a crunchy texture.

records.name: butter
records.description: BUTTER is a dairy product with high butterfat content which is solid when chilled and at room temperature in some regions, and liquid when warmed. It is made by churning fresh or fermented cream or milk to separate the butterfat from the buttermilk. It is generally used as a spread on plain or toasted bread products and a condiment on cooked vegetables, as well as in cooking, such as baking, sauce making, and pan frying.

records.name: butterfat
records.description: BUTTERFAT - the fatty portion of milk.

records.name: butterfish
records.description: Butterfish is the common name for a couple of different fish species, most notably: Escolar (Lepidocybium flavobrunneum) — sometimes marketed as "butterfish," this deep-sea fish has an extremely high oil content that gives it a rich, buttery texture and mouthfeel, hence the name. It's popular in sushi restaurants (sometimes mislabeled as "white tuna"); American butterfish (Peprilus triacanthus) — a smaller, silvery fish found along the U.S. Atlantic coast.

records.name: buttermilk
records.description: BUTTERMILK was the liquid left behind after churning butter out of cultured cream.

records.name: button mushroom
records.description: Button mushroom and white mushroom both refer to young Agaricus bisporus, harvested early before the cap opens up. "Button" describes the shape/size (small, round, unopened cap), while "white" describes the color strain.

records.name: cake
records.description: CAKE is a form of sweet food that is usually baked. The most commonly used cake ingredients include flour, sugar, eggs, butter or oil or margarine, a liquid, and leavening agents, such as baking soda or baking powder.

records.name: calf rennet
records.description: CALF RENNET is extracted from the inner mucosa of the fourth stomach chamber (the abomasum) of young, unweaned calves as part of livestock butchering.

records.name: Camargue whole long grain black rice
aliases: camargue whole long grain black rice

records.name: camelina oil
records.description: CAMELINA sativa is a flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae and is usually known in English as camelina. The crop is being researched due to its exceptionally high level (up to 45%) of omega-3 fatty acids, which is uncommon in vegetable sources.

records.name: camembert
records.description: CAMEMBERT is a moist, soft, creamy, surface-ripened cow's milk cheese from Normandy, France.

records.name: cane sugar
records.description: Since the 6th century BC, cane sugar producers have crushed the harvested vegetable material from sugarcane in order to collect and filter the juice. They then treat the liquid (often with lime (calcium oxide)) to remove impurities and then neutralize it. Boiling the juice then allows the sediment to settle to the bottom for dredging out, while the scum rises to the surface for skimming off.

records.name: canola oil
records.description: Canola oil, or canola for short, originally known as low erucic acid rapeseed, is a vegetable oil derived from a variety of rapeseed bred in Canada (Saskatchewan and Manitoba, 1960s-1970s) to be low in erucic acid, as opposed to colza oil.

records.name: cantal
records.description: Cantal cheese is an uncooked firm cheese produced in the Auvergne region of central France.

records.name: Cantal cheese half matured from cow's milk
aliases: cantal cheese half matured from cows milk

records.name: cantaloupe
records.description: Cantaloupe (muskmelon, mushmelon, rockmelon, sweet melon) or spanspek (South Africa) is a variety of the Cucumis melo species in the Cucurbitaceae family.

records.name: capelin
records.description: The capelin or caplin (Mallotus villosus) is a small forage fish of the smelt family found in the North Atlantic, North Pacific, and Arctic oceans. Commercialement, le capelan est utilisé comme produit alimentaire, et dans l'industrie des huiles de poisson. Sa chair a un goût agréable, ressemblant à celle du hareng. Les œufs de capelan ("masago") sont des produits alimentaires coûteux.

records.name: capsicum oleoresin
records.description: Capsicum Oleoresin is a highly concentrated capsicum extract.

records.name: caraway
records.description: CARAWAY (Carum carvi), is a biennial plant in the family Apiaceae. The fruits, usually used whole, have a pungent, anise-like flavor. Caraway is used as a spice in breads, especially rye bread. Caraway is also used in desserts, liquors, casseroles, and other foods.

records.name: carbonated water
records.description: Carbonated water is water infused with dissolved carbon dioxide gas under pressure, either occurring naturally in mineral springs—historically prized in spa towns like Perrier in France—or produced artificially through mechanical carbonation, a process commercialized in the late 18th century. It has a neutral base flavor with a distinctive sharp, slightly acidic bite and effervescent tingle from the carbonic acid formed as CO2 dissolves, and a lively, fizzy texture that fades once opened. Used as a refreshing standalone drink, a mixer in cocktails, and a base for flavored sodas, carbonated water contains no calories, protein, fat, or carbohydrates, and offers the same trace minerals as its source water, with no meaningful nutritional difference from still water beyond the carbonation itself.

records.name: caribou
records.description: "Caribou" is the term used in North America (Canada, Alaska) for wild populations. "Reindeer" is used in Europe and Asia, and also refers to the domesticated populations found especially in places like Scandinavia and Russia.

records.name: carissa
records.description: Carissa (commonly known as natal plum) is a small, glossy red fruit native to southern Africa, particularly South Africa, growing on a spiny shrub traditionally used both as a food source and an ornamental hedge in its native range. It has a tart, slightly sweet flavor often compared to a mix of cranberry and strawberry, with a soft, juicy flesh surrounding small seeds, though the unripe fruit and other plant parts contain a milky sap that's toxic if consumed. Eaten fresh, or used in jams, jellies, and sauces once ripe, carissa is a good source of vitamin C and antioxidants, though it remains a minor, largely regional fruit outside southern Africa.

records.name: carnaroli rice
records.description: CARNAROLI is a medium-grained rice grown in the Pavia, Novara and Vercelli provinces of northern Italy. Carnaroli is used for making risotto, differing from the more common arborio rice due to its higher starch content and firmer texture, as well as having a longer grain.

records.name: carob bean
records.description: Carob pods are mildly sweet on their own, so they are used in powdered, chip or syrup form as an ingredient in cakes and cookies, sometimes as a substitute for chocolate in recipes because of the color, texture, and taste of carob.

records.name: carob seed flour
records.description: Locust bean gum is produced from the endosperm, which accounts for 42–46% of the carob seed

records.name: carotenoids
records.description: Carotenoids are yellow, orange, and red organic pigments that are produced by plants and algae, as well as several bacteria and fungi. Carotenoids from the diet are stored in the fatty tissues of animals. There is insufficient evidence to state that carotenoids have an antioxidant function in humans or that carotenoid dietary supplements lower the risk of or prevent diseases.

records.name: carp
records.description: Carp is a freshwater fish that's been eaten by humans for thousands of years — it's actually one of the oldest farmed food fish in the world, with cultivation going back to ancient China. Taste and texture: Mild, slightly sweet, and somewhat earthy or "muddy" tasting, especially if it comes from murky water. Farm-raised carp raised in cleaner water tends to taste better. The flesh is firm but has a lot of small bones, similar to other freshwater fish like pike.

records.name: carrot
records.description: The CARROT (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) is a root vegetable, usually orange in colour, though purple, black, red, white, and yellow cultivars exist

records.name: Casein
records.description: Casein is the primary protein found in milk, making up about 80% of milk's protein content, and has been used for centuries in cheese-making across dairy-producing regions worldwide, since it's the protein that coagulates to form curds. It has a neutral, mildly milky flavor with no strong aroma, and forms a thick, slow-digesting texture when consumed—clumping into a gel in the stomach, unlike whey which stays liquid. Widely used in cheese production and as a slow-release protein supplement (particularly popular before bed among athletes), casein is a complete protein containing all nine essential amino acids, along with calcium and phosphorus from its dairy origin.

records.name: caseinate
records.description: Caseinate is a soluble form of casein—typically sodium or calcium caseinate—created by treating milk casein with an alkali to make it water-soluble, a processing method developed in the early-to-mid 20th century to allow casein's functional properties to be used more easily in manufactured foods. It has a neutral, mildly milky flavor with no strong aroma, and unlike regular casein, it dissolves smoothly in liquids and forms stable emulsions rather than clumping into curds. Widely used as an emulsifier and protein fortifier in coffee creamers, processed cheeses, and protein supplements, caseinate remains a complete protein containing all nine essential amino acids, along with calcium and phosphorus from its dairy origin.

records.name: cassia
records.description: Cinnamomum cassia, called Chinese cassia or Chinese cinnamon, is an evergreen tree originating in southern China

records.name: caster sugar
records.description: Caster sugar is finer than granulated sugar, but coarser than powdered/icing sugar, with a grain size of about 0.35 mm.

records.name: cauliflower
records.description: CAULIFLOWER is one of several vegetables in the species Brassica oleracea in the genus Brassica

records.name: cayenne pepper
records.description: The CAYENNE PEPPER is a type of Capsicum annuum. It is usually a moderately hot chili pepper used to flavor dishes.

records.name: celery
records.description: CELERY (Apium graveolens) is a marshland plant in the family Apiaceae that has been cultivated as a vegetable since antiquity.

records.name: cellulase
records.description: CELLULASE is any of several enzymes produced chiefly by fungi, bacteria, and protozoans that catalyze cellulolysis, the decomposition of cellulose and of some related polysaccharides. Cellulase is used for commercial food processing in coffee.

records.name: celtuce
records.description: Celtuce (also called stem lettuce, celery lettuce, or Chinese lettuce) is a vegetable that's actually a cultivar of the same species as regular lettuce (Lactuca sativa), but it's grown specifically for its thick, edible stem rather than its leaves. The stem has a mild, slightly sweet, and nutty flavor with a crisp, crunchy texture — often compared to a cross between celery, cucumber, and asparagus.

records.name: ceylon cinnamon
records.description: CINNAMOMUM VERUM, called true cinnamon tree or Ceylon cinnamon tree is a small evergreen tree belonging to the family Lauraceae, native to Sri Lanka.

records.name: champagne
records.description: Champagne is sparkling wine or, in the EU countries, legally only that sparkling wine which comes from the Champagne region of France.

records.name: champignon
records.description: AGARICUS BISPORUS is an edible basidiomycete mushroom native to grasslands in Europe and North America.

records.name: chard
records.description: CHARD (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris, Cicla-Group and Flavescens-Group) is a green leafy vegetable. Chard, like other green leafy vegetables, has highly nutritious leaves, making it a popular component of healthy diets.Fresh young chard can be used raw in salads. Mature chard leaves and stalks are typically cooked (like in pizzoccheri) or sautéed; the bitterness fades with cooking, leaving a refined flavor which is more delicate than that of cooked spinach.

records.name: chasselas
records.description: Chasselas or Chasselas blanc is a wine grape variety grown in Switzerland, France, Germany, Portugal, Hungary, Romania, New Zealand and Chile.

records.name: cheddar
records.description: CHEDDAR cheese is a relatively hard, off-white, sometimes sharp-tasting, natural cheese.

records.name: cheese
records.description: CHEESE is a dairy product derived from milk that is produced in a wide range of flavors, textures, and forms by coagulation of the milk protein casein.

records.name: cherry juice from concentrated cherry juice
aliases: cherry juice from concentrated cherry juice

records.name: chestnut
records.description: The chestnuts are a group of eight or nine species of deciduous trees and shrubs in the genus Castanea. The name also refers to the edible nuts they produce. The sweet chestnut produces an edible seed, the chestnut, which has been used in cooking since ancient times.

records.name: chestnut flour
records.description: Chestnuts can be dried and milled into flour, which can then be used to prepare breads, cakes, pies, pancakes, pastas, polenta, or used as thickener for stews, soups, and sauces.

records.name: chestnut mushroom
records.description: The mushroom commonly sold as "chestnut mushroom" is typically Pholiota adiposa (sometimes marketed varieties are hybrids/cultivars developed for the table), native to East Asia and popularized by Japanese cultivators.

records.name: chia
records.description: SALVIA HISPANICA, commonly known as CHIA, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae

records.name: chia seed
records.description: Native to Mexico and Guatemala, chia seeds come from the flowering plant Salvia hispanica. Black seeds are the traditional, more widely available variety; white seeds are a naturally occurring lighter variant, often prized for their appearance in pale-colored dishes. Both share a mild, nutty flavor and neutral taste, absorbing surrounding flavors easily. When soaked, they develop a gel-like texture, making them ideal for puddings, smoothies, baked goods, and as an egg substitute. Nutritionally identical, both are rich in fiber, plant-based omega-3s, protein, calcium, and antioxidants — a versatile, nutrient-dense addition to any diet.

records.name: chicken cutlet
records.description: Chicken Cutlet is a thin slice of meat from the leg or ribs of chicken.

records.name: chicken meat including natural chicken juices
aliases: chicken meat including natural chicken juices
chicken meat and natural chicken juices

records.name: chickpea
records.description: Chickpeas (Cicer arietinum), also known as garbanzo beans, are one of the world's oldest cultivated legumes, originating in the Middle East over 7,000 years ago and now grown widely across the Mediterranean, India, and the Americas. They have a mild, slightly nutty, earthy flavor with a firm yet creamy texture once cooked, making them extremely versatile in the kitchen. Chickpeas star in dishes like hummus, falafel, curries, soups, salads, and roasted snacks, and can be ground into flour for flatbreads and fritters. Nutritionally, they're a powerhouse: rich in plant-based protein, fiber, complex carbohydrates, iron, folate, and manganese, while being naturally low in fat. Their high fiber and protein content supports digestion, blood sugar stability, and satiety, making chickpeas a staple for vegetarian, vegan, and heart-healthy diets worldwide.

records.name: chicory greens
records.description: Chicory greens are the leafy tops (and sometimes tender inner leaves) of the chicory plant (Cichorium intybus), a bitter leafy vegetable in the same family as endive and radicchio. They're used in cooking much like other bitter greens — think dandelion greens or escarole. Distinctly bitter, with a slight earthiness. The bitterness mellows a lot when cooked.

records.name: chili powder
records.description: In the USDA FoodData Central database, chili powder is a seasoning blend, not a single-ingredient spice. It's typically listed as a blend of ground dried chili peppers combined with other spices — commonly cumin, oregano, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt, though blends vary by brand and recipe.

records.name: Chinese cabbage
records.description: Chinese cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. pekinensis) originated in East Asia, likely China, and has been cultivated for over 1,500 years before spreading worldwide. It features pale green, crinkled leaves with wide white ribs and a mild, slightly sweet flavor with subtle peppery notes. Globally, it's used in stir-fries, soups, dumplings, salads, and most famously as the base for Korean kimchi; it also appears in Japanese, Chinese, and Western cuisines as a crunchy, versatile vegetable. Nutritionally, it's low in calories and contains vitamins C and K, folate, potassium, and dietary fiber, along with various antioxidant compounds, making it a widely valued leafy vegetable across cultures.

records.name: chinese yam
records.description: Japanese mountain yam is native to China and Japan. Unlike most yams, it's often eaten raw — grated, it becomes sticky and mucilaginous (called tororo in Japanese cooking), used as a topping for rice, soba, or mixed into batters. It can also be cooked (steamed, boiled, fried).

records.name: chlorella
records.description: CHLORELLA is a genus of single-celled green algae belonging to the division Chlorophyta.

records.name: chocolate flavor filling with pieces of coconut
aliases: chocolate flavor filling with pieces of coconut

records.name: chocolate-flavored paste with ground cocoa biscuits
aliases: chocolate flavored paste with ground cocoa biscuits

records.name: chorizo
aliases: spicy pork sausage with red pepper no precision
records.description: CHORIZO or chouriço is a type of pork sausage. In Europe, chorizo is a fermented, cured, smoked sausage, which may be sliced and eaten without cooking, or added as an ingredient to add flavor to other dishes. Elsewhere, some sausages sold as chorizo may not be fermented and cured, and require cooking before eating. Spanish chorizo and Portuguese chouriço get their distinctive smokiness and deep red color from dried, smoked, red peppers.

records.name: chuck steak
records.description: CHUCK STEAK is a cut of beef and is part of the sub-prime cut known as the chuck.

records.name: churned butter
records.description: CHURNED BUTTER is butter churned in a butter churn to convert cream into butter.

records.name: cisco
records.description: Cisco is a freshwater whitefish in the genus Coregonus, found mainly in the Great Lakes and other cold lakes across North America (and some in Europe/Asia too). It's related to salmon and trout. Cisco  has a mild, delicate flavor — similar to other whitefish, slightly sweet. The texture is tender, flaky, fine-textured flesh — fairly delicate, can fall apart easily if overcooked.

records.name: citrus pectin
records.description: Modified citrus pectin (also known as CITRUS PECTIN, Pecta-Sol and MCP) is a modified, more digestible form of pectin. It is obtained from the peels, seeds and pulp of citrus fruits using a chemical extraction process.

records.name: Citrus unshiu
records.description: Citrus unshiu is a semi-seedless and easy-peeling citrus species, also known as miyagawa mandarin, unshu mikan, cold hardy mandarin, satsuma mandarin, satsuma orange, naartjie, and tangerine.

records.name: clarified butter
records.description: CLARIFIED BUTTER is milk fat rendered from butter to separate the milk solids and water from the butterfat

records.name: clove
records.description: CLOVEs are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum.

records.name: cocoa
records.description: Cocoa comes from the seeds (beans) of the cacao tree, native to Central and South America and used by the Aztecs and Maya for thousands of years in ceremonial and medicinal drinks long before it spread to Europe in the 16th century and became the basis for modern chocolate. It has a rich, bitter, complex flavor with earthy, fruity, and slightly astringent notes that vary by origin and processing, and comes in forms ranging from raw beans and nibs to fine cocoa powder, defined by its fat content (cocoa butter) after pressing. Used in chocolate-making, baking, and beverages, cocoa is notably rich in flavanol antioxidants, along with magnesium, iron, and fiber, though its bitter compounds are often offset with added sugar in most commercial products.

records.name: cocoa butter
records.description: COCOA BUTTER is a pale-yellow, edible vegetable fat extracted from the cocoa bean. Cocoa butter is a major ingredient in practically all types of chocolates (white chocolate, milk chocolate, and dark chocolate).

records.name: cocoa powder with reduced cocoa butter content
aliases: cocoa powder with reduced cocoa butter content

records.name: coconut oil
records.description: COCONUT OIL, or copra oil, is an edible oil extracted from the kernel or meat of mature coconuts harvested from the coconut palm (Cocos nucifera).

records.name: coconut sugar
records.description: COCONUT SUGAR is a palm sugar produced from the sap of the flower bud stem of the coconut palm. It is used in savory dishes, but mainly in local desserts and cakes of the Southeast Asian region. Coconut sugar is subtly sweet almost like brown sugar but with a slight hint of caramel. The flavor and sweetness is usually similar to table sugar or brown sugar. There is no scientific evidence that coconut sugar is more nutritious or healthier than any other sweetener.

records.name: coconut water made from concentrate coconut water
aliases: coconut water made from concentrate coconut water

records.name: Colby cheese
records.description: Type of semi-hard cheese.

records.name: collagen
records.description: COLLAGEN is the main structural protein in the extracellular space in the various connective tissues in the body.  It is widely used in the form of collagen casings for sausages, which are also used in the manufacture of musical strings.

records.name: collard greens
records.description: Collards (collard greens) are a leafy green vegetable in the cabbage family — the same species as kale, cabbage, and broccoli (Brassica oleracea), just bred for large, loose, dark green leaves rather than a tight head. Earthy, slightly bitter, and hearty — milder than mustard greens, tougher and more assertive than spinach. Traditionally slow-cooked (often with smoked meat, onion, garlic, vinegar, and pepper flakes in Southern U.S. cooking) until tender — but they can also be sautéed, steamed, or even eaten raw/massaged in salads if sliced thin. It's the same species as cabbage (Brassica oleracea), but not a cabbage in the way we normally mean the word.

records.name: colza oil
records.description: Colza oil or colza is a non-drying oil obtained from the seeds of rapeseed (Brassica napus subsp. napus).

records.name: common dentex
records.description: The common dentex (Dentex dentex) is a species of fish in the family Sparidae. Dentex is common in the Mediterranean Sea, but also seen in the Black Sea and the Eastern Atlantic Ocean from the British Isles to Mauritania.

records.name: common ling
records.description: This is a long, eel-like fish in the cod family (Gadidae), found in the North Atlantic, particularly around European and North American coasts. It has: A firm, white, flaky flesh similar to cod or haddock; A mild, slightly sweet flavor;A long, slender body (can grow quite large, sometimes over a meter)

records.name: common sole
records.description: The common sole, Dover sole, or black sole (Solea solea) is a species of flatfish in the family Soleidae.It is a largest fish in solea (fish) genus. Chefs prize Dover sole for its mild, buttery, sweet flavour and versatility, and for its ease of filleting.

records.name: Comté
records.description: COMTÉ (or Gruyère de Comté) is a French cheese made from unpasteurized cow's milk in the Franche-Comté region of eastern France.

records.name: concentrate
records.description: CONCENTRATE is the form of substance which has had the majority of its base component (in the case of a liquid: the solvent) removed

records.name: Cooked minced beef steak with 10% fat
aliases: cooked minced beef steak with 10 fat

aliases: cooked minced beef steak with 20 fat
