records.name: coriander
records.description: Coriander (Coriandrum sativum), also known as cilantro or Chinese parsley, is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.

records.name: Corinthian raisins
records.description: Zante currants are small, dried, seedless grapes — despite the name, they're not actually related to fresh currants (which are berries from the Ribes genus). Dried fruits made from the Black Corinth grape.

records.name: corn
records.description: Corn flour comes from maize, a grain domesticated in southern Mexico around 9,000 years ago and later becoming a dietary cornerstone across the Americas, from Mexican tortillas to Southern U.S. cornbread. It has a mild, slightly sweet, distinctly corn flavor with a fine, slightly gritty texture that lends baked goods a tender crumb and golden color. Naturally gluten-free, corn flour offers decent fiber and is a good source of B vitamins and antioxidants like lutein and zeaxanthin, though its protein is incomplete and lower in quality compared to grains like quinoa.

records.name: corn oil
records.description: Corn oil (maize oil) is oil extracted from the germ of corn (maize).

records.name: corn starch
records.description: Corn starch or maize starch is the starch derived from the corn (maize) grain.

records.name: Cotija cheese
records.description: type of dry, firm grating cheese from Mexico.

records.name: cottonseed
records.description: Cottonseed is the seed of the cotton plant (genus Gossypium), harvested as a byproduct of cotton fiber production. After cotton bolls are picked, the fluffy fiber (lint) is separated from the seeds during a process called ginning. Each cotton boll contains several seeds embedded in the fiber. Raw cottonseed contains a natural compound called gossypol, which is toxic to humans in significant quantities. Some specialty "glandless" cotton varieties have been bred to have naturally low gossypol levels, and these are sometimes explored as a protein source (the seed kernel is fairly protein-rich), but this isn't mainstream or widely available commercially.

records.name: cottonseed oil
records.description: COTTONSEED OIL is a cooking oil extracted from the seeds of cotton plants of various species

records.name: cow's milk
records.description: COW MILK - raw cow milk that probably has been treated (pasteurisation)

records.name: cowpea
records.description: Cowpeas (Vigna unguiculata), also known as black-eyed peas or southern peas, originated in West Africa thousands of years ago before spreading to the Mediterranean, Asia, and the Americas via trade and slavery routes. They have an earthy, mildly nutty flavor with a creamy texture once cooked. Versatile in the kitchen, they're used in stews, salads, fritters (like akara), rice dishes (such as Hoppin' John), and purees. Nutritionally, cowpeas are a powerhouse: high in plant-based protein and fiber, rich in folate, iron, magnesium, and potassium, and naturally low in fat—making them a staple for heart-healthy, budget-friendly diets worldwide.

records.name: crab
records.description: CRABS are decapod crustaceans of the infraorder Brachyura, which typically have a very short projecting "tail".

records.name: cranberry
records.description: Cranberries come in two main varieties: the American cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon), native to North America and long used by Indigenous peoples before becoming a major commercial crop in states like Massachusetts and Wisconsin, and the smaller European cranberry (Vaccinium oxycoccos), native to boggy regions across Northern Europe and Asia and traditionally foraged rather than farmed. Both have a sharply tart, astringent flavor with a firm, crisp bite when fresh, though the European variety tends to be smaller and even more tart than its larger American cousin. Eaten fresh, dried, juiced, or made into sauces, cranberries are notably rich in antioxidants, vitamin C, and compounds linked to urinary tract health, making them valued more for their functional benefits than their raw palatability.

records.name: crayfish
records.description: CRAYFISH, also known as crawfish, crawdads, crawlfish,[1] crawldads,[2] freshwater lobsters, mountain lobsters, mudbugs, or yabbies, are freshwater crustaceans resembling small lobsters

records.name: cream
records.description: CREAM is a dairy product composed of the higher-butterfat layer skimmed from the top of milk before homogenization.

records.name: cream with 10% milk fat
records.description: "Half and half" is a US product — equal parts whole milk and light cream, legally required to be at least 10.5% milkfat (usually closer to 10.5–18%).

records.name: cream with 36% milk fat
records.description: Under FDA standard of identity, 21 CFR §131.150: heavy cream is cream containing not less than 36 percent milkfat, and it must be pasteurized or ultra-pasteurized, with homogenization optional.

records.name: crème fraîche
records.description: Crème fraîche is a dairy product, a soured cream, with a pH of approximately 4.5. It is soured with a bacterial culture. European labeling regulations disallow any ingredients other than cream and bacterial culture. Fat percentage is more than 30%

records.name: Crottin de Chavignol cheese
aliases: crottin de chavignol cheese from goats milk
records.description: Crottin de Chavignol is a goat cheese produced in the Loire Valley.

records.name: crouton
records.description: A CROUTON is a piece of sautéed or rebaked bread, often cubed and seasoned, that is used to add texture and flavor to salads as an accompaniment to soups and stews, or eaten as a snack food.

records.name: crudités
records.description: Crudités (plural only) are traditional French appetizers consisting of sliced or whole raw vegetables[1] which are typically dipped in a vinaigrette or other dipping sauce. Examples of crudités include celery sticks, carrot sticks, cucumber sticks, bell pepper strips, broccoli, cauliflower, fennel, and asparagus spears.

records.name: cucumber
records.description: CUCUMBER (Cucumis sativus) is a widely cultivated plant in the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae.

records.name: cultured sour cream
records.description: Cultured sour cream is the standard, "real" sour cream — cream that's been fermented with bacterial cultures to develop its characteristic tang and thickness, as opposed to "acidified sour cream," which is soured artificially with food-grade acids instead of live cultures.

records.name: curing salt
records.description: CURING SALT is used in meat processing to generate a pinkish shade and to extend shelf life.

records.name: curry paste
records.description: CURRY PASTE usually refers to a paste used as a cooking ingredient in the preparation of a curry.

records.name: curry powder
records.description: CURRY POWDER is a spice mix originating from the Indian subcontinent.

records.name: cusk
records.description: Cusk (Brosme brosme) is a bottom-dwelling fish in the cod family (Gadidae), found in the cold waters of the North Atlantic — off the coasts of New England, Atlantic Canada, and northern Europe. Cusk has firm, white flesh similar to cod or haddock, and is prized by some for its mild flavor. It's often sold fresh or used in chowders.

records.name: dark chocolate
records.description: DARK BLACK CHOCOLATE is a form of chocolate containing cocoa solids, cocoa butter and sugar, without the milk found in milk chocolate.

records.name: dark syrup
records.description: Dark syrup is similar to a mix of golden syrup and black treacle, being thinner and with a less pronounced flavour than that of black treacle.

records.name: date
records.description: DATE, the fruit of the date palm (Phoenix dactylifera). Dry or soft dates are eaten out-of-hand, or may be pitted and stuffed with fillings such as almonds, walnuts, pecans, candied orange and lemon peel, tahini, marzipan or cream cheese.

records.name: dehydrated poultry fond
aliases: poultry stock for sauce and cooking dehydrated

records.name: dijon mustard
records.description: A kind of mustard made with verjuice (or, more recently, white wine) instead of vinegar.

records.name: dill
records.description: dill (anethum graveolens) is an annual herb in the celery family apiaceae. dill is widely grown in eurasia where its leaves and seeds are used as a herb or spice for flavouring food.

records.name: dishcloth
records.description: "Dishcloth gourd" (also called towel gourd, sponge gourd, or luffa) is the common name for Luffa — usually Luffa aegyptiaca (smooth luffa) or Luffa acutangula (angled/ridged luffa, sometimes called "Chinese okra"). It's a tropical vine in the cucumber/squash family, common in Asian, African, and some Mediterranean cuisines. The flesh is mild, slightly sweet, and a bit like a cross between zucchini and cucumber, with a spongy texture that softens when cooked.

records.name: dock
records.description: Dock (genus Rumex, especially curly dock — Rumex crispus — and broad-leaved dock — Rumex obtusifolius) is a wild edible plant. Young leaves have a tart, lemony, slightly sour flavor thanks to oxalic acid — similar to sorrel but a bit milder. As leaves mature they get tougher and more bitter/astringent. Young leaves: eaten raw in salads, or added to soups, stews, and sautés like spinach.; Older leaves: usually cooked (boiled or braised) to mellow the sourness and soften the texture.

records.name: Double Gloucester
records.description: Gloucester is a traditional, semi-hard cheese which has been made in Gloucestershire, England, since the 16th century, at one time made only with the milk of the once nearly extinct Gloucester cattle.

records.name: drumstick leaves
records.description: Small, oval-shaped leaflets of the moringa tree (Moringa oleifera), sometimes called the horseradish tree or ben tree. The leaves grow in clusters on the branches, often described as feathery or fern-like in arrangement. They're a popular vegetable in South Asian, Southeast Asian, and African cuisines. Added to salads, or cooked briefly like spinach — sautéed, added to soups, dals, or stir-fries.

records.name: drumstick pods
records.description: "Drumstick" is the common name for the long, slender seed pods of the moringa tree (Moringa oleifera), sometimes called the horseradish tree or ben tree. They're a popular vegetable in South Asian, Southeast Asian, and African cuisines. Long, thin, ridged green pods, often 1–3 feet long. Mild, slightly sweet, a bit like asparagus or green beans.

records.name: dry tapioca pearls
records.description: Tapioca pearls are made from cassava root starch, a plant native to South America but now cultivated widely across Brazil, Southeast Asia, and Africa. On their own, dry pearls are essentially flavorless and starchy, taking on a mild sweetness and chewy, translucent texture once cooked. They're most commonly used in bubble tea, puddings, and Southeast Asian desserts, or as a thickener in soups and pie fillings. Nutritionally, tapioca is mostly pure carbohydrate with very little protein, fiber, or micronutrients, making it a gluten-free energy source but not a significant source of other nutrients.

records.name: dry-grilled and unsalted cashew nut
aliases: dry grilled and unsalted cashew nut

records.name: dulse
records.description: Palmaria palmata, also called dulse, dillisk or dilsk (from Irish/Scottish Gaelic duileasc/duileasg), red dulse, sea lettuce flakes, or creathnach, is a red alga (Rhodophyta) previously referred to as Rhodymenia palmata.

records.name: durian
records.description: Durian is a large, spiky tropical fruit native to Southeast Asia, particularly Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand, where it's been cultivated for centuries and earned the nickname "king of fruits" despite—or because of—its notoriously divisive smell. It has a custardy, rich, creamy texture with a complex flavor often described as a blend of sweet caramel, almond, and savory onion notes, paired with a famously pungent, sulfurous odor strong enough to be banned on public transport in parts of Southeast Asia. Eaten fresh or used in desserts, candies, and ice cream, durian is notably rich in healthy fats, fiber, vitamin C, and potassium, making it more calorie-dense and nutritious than most other fruits.

records.name: durum wheat
records.description: Durum wheat (Triticum durum or Triticum turgidum subsp. durum) is a tetraploid species of wheat.

records.name: edam
records.description: EDAM is a semi-hard cheese that originated in the Netherlands, and is named after the town of Edam in the province of North Holland.

records.name: edible coating originating from bovine collagen
aliases: edible coating originating from bovine collagen

records.name: edible-podded pea
records.description: The edible-podded pea (Pisum sativum var. saccharatum) are a variety of pea eaten whole in its pod while still unripe.

records.name: egg
records.description: EGGS are laid by female animals of many different species, including birds, reptiles, amphibians, mammals, and fish. This ingredient comprises mainly chicken eggs.

records.name: egg white
records.description: EGG WHITE is the clear liquid (also called the albumen or the glair/glaire) contained within an egg.

records.name: eggs yolk powder from free range hens
aliases: eggs yolk powder from free range hens

records.name: emmental
records.description: EMMENTAL (Emmentaler or Emmenthal) is a yellow, medium-hard Swiss cheese that originated in the area around Emmental, Canton Bern.

records.name: endive
records.description: Cichorium endivia is a species of flowering plant belonging to the genus Cichorium, which is widely cultivated as one of the species of similar bitter-leafed vegetables known as endive and escarole.

records.name: Enoki mushrooms
records.description: Enoki mushrooms (also called enokitake, golden needle mushrooms, or velvet shank) are a type of edible mushroom (Flammulina velutipes or filiformis) commonly used in East Asian cuisine, especially Japanese, Korean, and Chinese cooking. Mild, slightly sweet, and faintly fruity flavor; crisp, crunchy texture, even after cooking; Often described as having a delicate, almost noodle-like quality

records.name: enzyme
records.description: ENZYME - is a macromolecular biological catalysts. Enzymes accelerate chemical reactions.

records.name: epazote
records.description: Epazote (Dysphania ambrosioides, formerly Chenopodium ambrosioides) is a pungent, aromatic herb widely used in Mexican and Central American cooking. The flavor is hard to pin down — people describe it as a mix of citrus, mint, anise, tar, and even petroleum-like notes. It's strong, so it's used in moderation, usually just a sprig or a few leaves per dish, added toward the end of cooking to preserve its aroma. Epazote contains compounds (like ascaridole) that can be toxic in concentrated amounts, such as in essential oil form. Using fresh or dried leaves in normal cooking quantities is considered safe and is how it's traditionally consumed — but it shouldn't be consumed as a concentrated extract or in medicinal "high dose" preparations.

records.name: eppaw
records.description: Eppaw is the edible tuber of the duck potato plant (Sagittaria latifolia, also called wapato or arrowhead), traditionally eaten by some Native American groups, particularly noted in Seminole/Florida contexts. It's a starchy, potato-like root vegetable that grows in shallow water and marshes, and was historically gathered as a wild food source.

records.name: Espelette chili pepper
records.description: The Espelette pepper is a variety of Capsicum annuum that is cultivated in the French commune of Espelette, Pyrénées-Atlantiques, traditionally the northern territory of the Basque people. On 1 June 2000, it was classified as an AOC product and was confirmed as an APO product on 22 August 2002.

records.name: essential oil
records.description: ESSENTIAL OIL is a concentrated hydrophobic liquid containing volatile aroma compounds from plants.

records.name: ethanol
records.description: ETHANOL, also called alcohol, ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol, and drinking alcohol, is a chemical compound, a simple alcohol with the chemical formula C2H5OH.

records.name: eucalyptus oil
records.description: EUCALYPTUS OIL is the generic name for distilled oil from the leaf of Eucalyptus, a genus of the plant family Myrtaceae native to Australia and cultivated worldwide. Eucalyptus oil has a history of wide application, as a pharmaceutical, antiseptic, repellent, flavouring, fragrance and industrial uses.

records.name: European anchovy
records.description: The European anchovy (Engraulis encrasicolus) is a forage fish somewhat related to the herring.

records.name: European perch
records.description: The European perch (Perca fluviatilis), also known as the common perch, redfin perch, big-scaled redfin, English perch, Eurasian perch, Eurasian river perch, Hatch or in Anglophone parts of Europe, simply the perch, is a predatory species of the freshwater perch native to Europe and northern Asia.

records.name: European plaice
records.description: The European plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) is a commercially important flatfish

records.name: European seabass
records.description: The European bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) is a primarily ocean-going fish native to the waters off Europe's western and southern and Africa's northern coasts.

records.name: evaporated milk
records.description: EVAPORATED MILK, known in some countries as "unsweetened condensed milk", is a shelf-stable canned milk product with about 60% of the water removed from fresh milk. It differs from sweetened condensed milk, which contains added sugar. Sweetened condensed milk requires less processing since the added sugar inhibits bacterial growth.

records.name: extra old Mimolette
aliases: extra old mimolette cheese from cows milk

records.name: extract
records.description: An extract is a substance made by extracting a part of a raw material, often by using a solvent such as ethanol or water. Extracts may be sold as tinctures, absolutes or in powder form.

records.name: faiselle
records.description: Faisselle is a non-protected French cheese made of raw milk from cows, goats, or sheep.

records.name: fat
records.description: FAT is one of the three main macronutrients, along with the other two:carbohydrate and protein. Fats molecules consist of primarily carbon and hydrogen atoms, thus they are all hydrocarbon molecules.

records.name: fat free half and half cream
aliases: fat free half and half cream
records.description: Fat-free half and half is a bit of a paradox from a US regulatory standpoint. Real "half and half" has a legal minimum milkfat content — the standards of identity for half-and-half fall under 21 CFR Part 131, and specifically §131.180 sets the minimum at 10.5% milkfat. So it's technically an imitation or substitute product

records.name: fat reduced cocoa powder
aliases: cocoa powder with low fat content

records.name: feijoa
records.description: Feijoa (Acca sellowiana) is a fruit native to South America — specifically the highlands of southern Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay, and northern Argentina. The flavour is distinctive and hard to compare — often described as a mix of pineapple, guava, mint, and strawberry, with floral notes. The flesh inside is creamy white and slightly gritty near the center, similar to a ripe pear.

records.name: fennel
records.description: FENNEL (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family. The bulb, foliage, and fruits of the fennel plant are used in many of the culinary traditions of the world. The bulb is a crisp vegetable that can be sautéed, stewed, braised, grilled, or eaten raw. Young tender leaves are used for garnishes, as a salad, to add flavor to salads, to flavor sauces to be served with puddings, and also in soups and fish sauce.

records.name: ferment
records.description: FERMENT is an agent, such as an enzyme, bacterium, or fungus, that brings about fermentation.

records.name: feta
records.description: FETA is a greek brined curd white cheese from sheep's milk or from a mixture of sheep and goat's milk.

records.name: fiddlehead fern
records.description: Fiddlehead ferns are the tightly coiled, immature fronds of certain fern species, harvested in early spring before they unfurl. They're named for their resemblance to the curled end (scroll) of a fiddle or violin. Most common edible variety: Ostrich fern (Matteuccia struthiopteris) is the safest and most widely eaten species. Not all fern fiddleheads are edible — some are toxic, so identification matters. Often described as a cross between asparagus, green beans, and a slightly nutty, grassy taste. Fiddleheads must be cooked thoroughly (boiled or steamed for several minutes, then sautéed if desired) before eating. Raw or undercooked fiddleheads have caused foodborne illness outbreaks — they can carry bacteria or contain compounds that cause nausea, cramps, and diarrhea if not properly prepared.

records.name: filmjölk
records.description: FILMJÖLK (Swedish: [ˈfîːlmjœlk]), also known as fil, is a traditional fermented milk product from Sweden, and a common dairy product within the Nordic countries. It is made by fermenting cow's milk with a variety of bacteria from the species Lactococcus lactis and Leuconostoc mesenteroides.

records.name: firewood leaf
records.description: Fireweed (Chamaenerion angustifolium, also called Epilobium angustifolium) is a tall wildflower with bright pink-purple flower spikes, common in northern temperate regions. Young leaves, picked before the plant flowers, can be eaten raw in salads or cooked like spinach. As the plant matures, the leaves get tougher and more bitter, so timing matters. Fireweed has a mild laxative effect in some people if eaten in quantity, so it's usually eaten in modest amounts rather than as a main dish.

records.name: First age baby milk powder
aliases: first infant milk formula in powder

records.name: fish
records.description: Fish are gill-bearing aquatic craniate animals that lack limbs with digits.

records.name: fish oil
records.description: FISH OIL is oil derived from the tissues of oily fish

records.name: flat bean
records.description: FLAT BEANS, also known as helda beans, romano beans and "gavar fhali" in some Indian states, are a variety of Phaseolus coccineus, known as runner bean with edible pods that have a characteristic wide and flat shape.

records.name: flat fish
records.description: Flat fish are a group of fish that live and swim mostly on the ocean floor, and their most striking feature is that their bodies are flattened sideways (laterally compressed) so they end up lying and swimming on one side rather than upright.

records.name: flat peach
records.description: The flat peach (Prunus persica var. platycarpa), also known as the doughnut peach or Saturn peach, is a variety of peach with pale yellow fruit that is oblate in shape.

records.name: flax seed
records.description: Flax, also known as common flax or linseed, is a flowering plant, Linum usitatissimum, in the family Linaceae. Flax seeds occur in two basic varieties/colors: brown or yellow (golden linseeds).

records.name: flaxseed oil with added sliced flaxseed
aliases: flaxseed oil with added sliced flaxseed

records.name: Fleur de sel
records.description: FLEUR DE SEL - is a salt that forms as a thin, delicate crust on the surface of seawater as it evaporates.

records.name: flour
records.description: FLOUR is a powder made by grinding raw grains or roots and used to make many different foods.

records.name: fontina
records.description: Fontina is a cow's milk cheese, produced worldwide.

records.name: fontina AOP
records.description: Fontina AOP is an cow's milk cheese, produced in the Aosta Valley.

records.name: fourme d'ambert
records.description: Fourme d'Ambert is a semi-hard French AOC blue cheese, made from raw cow's milk from the Auvergne region of France.

records.name: fourme de Montbrison
records.description: Fourme de Montbrison is a cow's-milk cheese made in the regions of Rhône-Alpes and Auvergne in southern France.

records.name: freekeh
records.description: Freekeh (sometimes spelled frikeh) or farik is a cereal food made from green durum wheat (Triticum turgidum var. durum) that is roasted and rubbed to create its flavour.

records.name: freshwater bream
records.description: Bream are species of freshwater and marine fish belonging to a variety of genera.

records.name: frillice iceberg lettuce
records.description: Frillice iceberg lettuce is a cross of curly endive and iceberg lettuce, with the taste and texture of iceberg and the frilly top of the curly endive.

records.name: fromage blanc
records.description: FROMAGE BLANC is a fresh cheese originating from the north of France and the south of Belgium.

records.name: frozen unprepared turnip green and turnip
aliases: frozen unprepared turnip green and turnip

records.name: Fructooligosaccharide
records.description: Fructooligosaccharide (FOS) is a short-chain fructan found naturally in foods like chicory root, onions, garlic, and bananas, and produced commercially either by extracting it from chicory or through enzymatic conversion of sucrose, with much of the technology developed in Japan and France. It has a mild sweetness, roughly 30-50% as sweet as sucrose, with a clean flavor and no notable aroma, and is used in food products as a low-calorie sweetener, texture enhancer, and fat replacer. Like oligofructose, FOS acts as a soluble prebiotic fiber that resists digestion in the small intestine and ferments in the colon to feed beneficial gut bacteria, providing fewer calories than sucrose while supporting digestive health.

records.name: fructose
records.description: Fructose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide) that occurs naturally in fruits, honey, and some vegetables, and is produced commercially either by processing corn starch into high-fructose corn syrup (mainly in the U.S.) or by refining it from sucrose. It has the sweetest taste of all natural sugars—notably sweeter than sucrose or glucose—with no notable aroma, and is used in beverages, baked goods, and processed foods both for its intense sweetness and its ability to enhance flavor and browning. Fructose provides purely empty calories with no fiber, vitamins, or minerals, and is metabolized differently than glucose—processed primarily by the liver—which has made it a focus of concern around excessive consumption and links to metabolic issues.

records.name: fruit
records.description: Fruit is the mature, seed-bearing structure of flowering plants, cultivated and foraged by humans since prehistoric times across virtually every inhabited region, with different varieties native to tropical, temperate, and Mediterranean climates worldwide. It has an enormously varied flavor and texture profile—from the crisp sweetness of apples to the juicy tang of citrus and the soft, custardy richness of tropical fruits like mango—generally balancing natural sugars with acidity. Eaten fresh, dried, juiced, or cooked into jams, desserts, and savory dishes, fruit is prized nutritionally for its fiber, vitamins (especially vitamin C), antioxidants, and natural sugars, making it a nutrient-dense counterpart to refined sweeteners.

records.name: fruit juices and purees from concentrate
aliases: fruit juices and purees from concentrate

records.name: Fucus
records.description: Fucus is a genus of brown algae found in the intertidal zones of rocky seashores almost throughout the world.

records.name: fuki
records.description: Fuki (Petasites japonicus) is a flowering plant native to Europe and parts of Asia and North America. In Japanese cuisine, fuki is a well-established vegetable and has been eaten for centuries: The leaf stalks (petioles) are the main edible part — boiled, then peeled and used in simmered dishes (nimono), stir-fries, or as a side dish; The flower buds (fuki no tō) are a beloved spring delicacy, eaten tempura-fried or as a miso paste — they have a pleasant, slightly bitter taste.

records.name: garland chrysanthemum
records.description: "Garland chrysanthemum" (also called tong ho in Chinese, shungiku in Japanese, and ssukgat in Korean) is an edible leafy green — not the ornamental flower you'd put in a bouquet, but a related plant (Glebionis coronaria) grown specifically for eating. Slightly bitter, herbal, and a little peppery — some describe it as tasting faintly like chrysanthemum tea smells.

records.name: Garofa nectarine
records.description: Yellow-fleshed early season nectarine variety.

records.name: gelatin
records.description: GELATIN or GELATINE is a translucent, colorless, brittle (when dry), flavorless food ingredient that is derived from collagen obtained from various animal body parts.

records.name: ghee
records.description: Ghee is a type of clarified butter that's especially common in South Asian and Indian cooking. It has a rich, nutty, slightly caramelized taste. It's used in Indian cooking (dals, curries, rice dishes), for frying, drizzling over flatbreads.

records.name: gherkin
records.description: GHERKIN can refer to either a pickled small cucumber (esp. in Ireland and the UK) or an unpickled small cucumber

records.name: gin
records.description: GIN is a distilled alcoholic drink that derives its predominant flavour from juniper berries.

records.name: ginger
records.description: GINGER (Zingiber officinale) is a flowering plant whose rhizome, ginger root or simply ginger, is widely used as a spice or a folk medicine

records.name: gingerbread
records.description: GINGERBREAD refers to a broad category of baked goods, typically flavored with ginger, cloves, nutmeg or cinnamon and sweetened with honey, sugar or molasses.

records.name: glasswort
records.description: Salicornia is a genus of succulent, halophyte (salt tolerant) flowering plants in the family Amaranthaceae that grow in salt marshes, on beaches, and among mangroves. The main European species is often eaten and the main North American species is occasionally sold in grocery stores or appears on restaurant menus, usually as 'sea beans' or samphire greens or sea asparagus.

records.name: glucose
records.description: Glucose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide) that occurs naturally in fruits, honey, and plants, and is produced commercially by breaking down starch—typically from corn in the U.S. or wheat and potatoes in Europe—through enzymatic or acid hydrolysis. It has a moderately sweet flavor, less sweet than sucrose or fructose, with no notable aroma, and is available as a syrup or dried/powdered form used widely in candy-making, baking, and brewing for its resistance to crystallization and browning properties. As the primary fuel source for the human body, glucose provides purely caloric energy with no fiber, vitamins, or minerals, and it's the sugar that directly raises blood glucose levels, giving it the highest glycemic index among common sugars.

records.name: Glycerol monostearate
records.description: GLYCEROL MONOSTEARATE, commonly known as GMS, is a monoglyceride commonly used as an emulsifier in foods. GMS is a food additive used as a thickening, emulsifying, anticaking, and preservative agent; an emulsifying agent for oils, waxes, and solvents; a protective coating for hygroscopic powders; a solidifier and control release agent in pharmaceuticals; and a resin lubricant.

records.name: goat cheese
records.description: GOAT CHEESE, goats' cheese, or chèvre, is cheese made from goat's milk.

records.name: goat meat
records.description: GOAT MEAT or goat's meat is the meat of the domestic goat (Capra aegagrus hircus). Goat meat is savory and less sweet than beef[9] but slightly sweeter than lamb. It can be prepared in a variety of ways, such as being stewed, curried, baked, grilled, barbecued, minced, canned, fried, or made into sausage. Goat jerky is also another popular variety.

records.name: goat milk
records.description: Goat milk is the milk of domestic goats.

records.name: golden chanterelle
records.description: CANTHARELLUS CIBARIUS is a species of golden chanterelle mushroom in the genus Cantharellus.

records.name: gorgonzola
records.description: GORGONZOLA is a veined Italian blue cheese, made from unskimmed cow's milk.

records.name: gouda
records.description: GOUDA is a mild, yellow cheese made from cow's milk.

records.name: Grana Padano
aliases: grana padano cheese from cows milk
records.description: GRANA PADANO is a hard, slow-ripened, semi-fat, cow's-milk cheese from Italy.

records.name: granulated sugar
records.description: Granulated, familiar as table sugar, with a grain size about 0.5-0.6 mm across.

records.name: grape
records.description: A grape is a fruit, botanically a berry, of the deciduous woody vines of the flowering plant genus Vitis.

records.name: grape juice
records.description: Grape juice is obtained from crushing and blending grapes into a liquid.

records.name: grape juice from concentrate
records.description: This is a compound product made of concentrate grape juice and water.

records.name: grape leaf
records.description: Grape leaves (also called vine leaves) are the young, tender leaves of the grape plant (Vitis vinifera), used as a vegetable or wrap in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, Balkan, and Caucasian cooking rather than eaten as a leafy green on their own. Slightly tart, earthy, a bit lemony — this comes mostly from the way they're brined or cooked (often with lemon juice).

records.name: grape seed oil
records.description: GRAPE SEED OIL (also called grapeseed oil or grape oil) is pressed from the seeds of grapes, and is thus an abundant by-product of winemaking.

records.name: grapefruit or pomelo juice from concentrate
aliases: grapefruit or pomelo juice from concentrate

records.name: grated emmental cheese
aliases: emmental cheese grated from cows milk

records.name: Greenland halibut
records.description: The Greenland halibut or Greenland turbot (Reinhardtius hippoglossoides) belongs to the family Pleuronectidae.

records.name: grouper
records.description: Groupers are fish of any of a number of genera in the subfamily Epinephelinae of the family Serranidae, in the order Perciformes.

records.name: gruyère
records.description: Gruyere is a hard cheese mad from cow milk. It originates either from Switzerland or France.

records.name: gruyère AOP
records.description: GRUYÈRE is a hard yellow cheese that originated in the cantons of Fribourg, Vaud, Neuchâtel, Jura, and Bern in Switzerland.

records.name: gruyere pgi
aliases: gruyere cheese france protected geographical indication from cows milk

records.name: gum base
records.description: GUM BASE is the non-nutritive, non-digestible, water-insoluble masticatory delivery system used to carry sweeteners, flavors, and any other substances in chewing gum and bubble gum. It provides all the basic textural and masticatory properties of gum. The actual composition of gum base is usually a trade secret.

records.name: haddock
records.description: Haddock is a saltwater fish, closely related to cod and are found mainly in the North Atlantic. Flavor and texture: Mild, slightly sweet flavor with white, flaky flesh. It's often described as a bit more delicate than cod. It's the classic fish used in British fish and chips

records.name: half-old Mimolette
aliases: half old mimolette cheese from cows milk

records.name: halloumi
records.description: HALLOUMI or haloumi is a semi-hard, unripened, brined cheese made from a mixture of goat's and sheep's milk, and sometimes also cow's milk.

records.name: hard red spring wheat
records.description: Hard red spring wheat is grown mainly in the northern U.S. Great Plains and Canada, planted in spring and harvested in fall due to the region's harsh winters. It has a robust, nutty, earthy flavor, generally considered slightly more pronounced than winter wheat varieties. Its very high protein and gluten content make it prized for artisan breads, bagels, and pizza dough that require strong structure and chew. Nutritionally, it's rich in protein, fiber, and B vitamins, especially when milled as whole grain.

records.name: hard red winter wheat
records.description: Hard red winter wheat is grown extensively across the U.S. Great Plains, planted in fall and harvested in early summer, making it one of the most widely cultivated wheat classes in the world. It has a robust, slightly nutty, earthy flavor with more depth than white wheat varieties. Its high protein and gluten content make it a top choice for yeasted breads, as well as all-purpose and bread flours. Nutritionally, it's rich in protein, fiber, and B vitamins, especially when milled as whole grain.

records.name: hard white wheat
records.description: Hard white wheat is a relatively modern variety, developed and popularized in the U.S. during the 20th century as a milder alternative to traditional red wheat. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor without the bitterness often found in red wheat varieties. Its high protein and gluten content make it well-suited for yeasted breads, while also working for pastries and tortillas. Nutritionally, it's a good source of protein, fiber, and B vitamins, particularly when milled as whole grain.

records.name: harissa
records.description: HARISSA is a Tunisian hot chili pepper paste, the main ingredients of which are roasted red peppers, Baklouti pepper, serrano peppers, and other hot chili peppers, spices and herbs such as garlic paste, coriander seed, saffron, rose, or caraway, as well as some vegetable or olive oil to carry the oil-soluble flavors.

records.name: Havarti
records.description: semisoft Danish cow's milk cheese.

records.name: hazelnut
records.description: The HAZELNUT is the nut of the hazel and therefore includes any of the nuts deriving from species of the genus Corylus, especially the nuts of the species Corylus avellana.

records.name: hazelnut paste with pieces of biscuits
aliases: hazelnut paste with pieces of biscuits

records.name: heart of palm
records.description: The heart of palm is the inner core of certain palm trees, harvested as a vegetable and typically canned or jarred in brine.

records.name: herring
records.description: A type of small, oily fish of the genus Clupea, often used as food.

records.name: hickorynut
records.description: A hickory nut is the edible nut produced by trees in the genus Carya — the same genus that includes pecans. They're native mostly to North America, with a few species in Asia. Encased in a thick, husk-like outer covering that splits open (fully or partially, depending on species) when ripe, revealing a hard shell. Inside that shell is the actual nutmeat. Flavor varies a lot by species — some, like shagbark hickory, are sweet and rich (similar to a pecan, which makes sense given the family connection), while others, like pignut hickory, can be bitter or astringent.

records.name: high fructose corn syrup
records.description: High-fructose corn syrup (HFCS) (also called glucose-fructose, isoglucose and glucose-fructose syrup) is a sweetener made from corn starch

records.name: high oleic sunflower oil (70% and over)
aliases: high oleic sunflower oil 70 and over

records.name: honey
records.description: HONEY is a sweet, viscous food substance produced by bees and some related insects.

records.name: honjozo
records.description: Honjōzō (本醸造, 'genuine fermented'): Contains 100% genuine fermented product

records.name: horned melon
records.description: The horned melon (kiwano) is a tropical fruit native to sub-Saharan Africa, though it's now grown in other warm regions like New Zealand, Australia, and California. The flavor is mild and refreshing — often described as a blend of cucumber, banana, and lime, with a slightly tart note.

records.name: horse gram
records.description: Native to South Asia, horse gram is an ancient, drought-resistant legume long cultivated across India, Nepal, and parts of Africa and Southeast Asia, where it's also used as livestock fodder. Small, flattish, and reddish-brown, it has a robust, earthy, slightly nutty flavor with a firm bite. Traditionally simmered into soups, stews, and sprouted dishes, or ground into flour, it's especially prized in South Indian cuisine (like kulith usal). Nutritionally, it stands out among pulses for its exceptional protein, iron, and calcium content, along with dietary fiber, making it a valued, if underappreciated, global superfood.

records.name: horse mackerel
records.description: Horse mackerel is a vague vernacular term for a range of species of fish throughout the English-speaking world.

records.name: horseradish
records.description: HORSERADISH (Armoracia rusticana, syn. Cochlearia armoracia) is a perennial plant of the family Brassicaceae. The intact horseradish root has hardly any aroma. When cut or grated enzymes from the now-broken plant cells break down sinigrin (a glucosinolate) to produce allyl isothiocyanate (mustard oil), which irritates the mucous membranes of the sinuses and eyes. Grated mash should be used immediately or preserved in vinegar for best flavor.

records.name: household hydrogenated soybean and palm shortening
aliases: household hydrogenated soybean and palm shortening

records.name: hulled barley
records.description: Hulled barley is a whole grain barley with only the inedible outer shell removed.

records.name: hungarian peppers
records.description: Hungarian peppers usually refers to a family of peppers most associated with Hungarian cuisine and paprika production. Tangy, slightly sweet, with a crisp bite — similar in style to a banana pepper but noticeably spicier.

records.name: hyacinth bean
records.description: Hyacinth beans (Lablab purpureus, also called lablab beans, dolichos beans, or Egyptian beans) are a fast-growing climbing vine grown both as an ornamental plant and a food crop. The young, immature pods can be cooked and eaten like green beans. However, the mature beans and pods contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be thoroughly cooked (usually boiled with water changes) before eating — they're toxic raw or undercooked. In parts of Africa and Asia, they're a significant food crop and protein source when properly prepared.

records.name: hydrogenated oil
records.description: Hydrogenation converts liquid vegetable oils into solid or semi-solid fats, such as those present in margarine. Changing the degree of saturation of the fat changes some important physical properties, such as the melting range, which is why liquid oils become semi-solid.

records.name: hydrogenated soybean and hydrogenated palm multipurpose shortening
aliases: hydrogenated soybean and hydrogenated palm multipurpose shortening

records.name: hydrogenated soybean palm and cottonseed shortening for baking
aliases: hydrogenated soybean palm and cottonseed shortening for baking

records.name: hydrogenated soybean shortening for cakes and frostings
aliases: hydrogenated soybean shortening for cakes and frostings

records.name: hydrolysed vegetable protein
records.description: Hydrolyzed vegetable protein (HVP) is a flavor enhancer made by chemically breaking down plant proteins—typically soy, corn, or wheat—using acid hydrolysis, a process developed in the early 20th century and widely adopted in industrial food manufacturing to create savory, meat-like flavors without meat. It has an intensely savory, umami-rich flavor with notes reminiscent of broth or bouillon, and comes as a fine powder or paste used in tiny quantities to boost taste. Commonly used in soups, sauces, snack seasonings, and processed foods as a cheaper alternative to natural flavor development, HVP contributes free glutamic acid (similar to MSG) along with trace amino acids, but is used in such small amounts that it offers negligible nutritional value beyond flavor enhancement.

records.name: ice
records.description: Ice is water in its solid state, forming when temperatures drop to or below 0°C (32°F), found naturally in glaciers, polar regions, and frost, and produced commercially or at home through refrigeration for use in food and beverages. It has no flavor or aroma of its own, taking on a hard, crystalline texture that can range from clear and dense to cloudy and brittle depending on freezing speed and mineral content. Used primarily for chilling drinks and food, preserving perishables, and in ice sculptures or winter sports, ice contains no calories, protein, fat, or carbohydrates, offering the same trace minerals as its source water but purely a physical, non-nutritive ingredient.

records.name: ice cream
records.description: ICE CREAM is a sweetened frozen food typically eaten as a snack or dessert. It may be made from dairy milk or cream, or soy, cashew, coconut or almondmilk, and is flavored with a sweetener, either sugar or an alternative, and any spice, such as cocoa or vanilla. Colourings are usually added, in addition to stabilizers.

records.name: illipe oil
records.description: ILLIPE butter is a vegetable fat from the nut of the Shorea stenoptera tree.

records.name: imazalil
records.description: Imazalil is a fungicide widely used in agriculture, particularly in the growing of citrus fruits.

records.name: Imleria
records.description: IMLERIA is a genus of mushrooms from the Boletaceae family

records.name: indian squid
records.description: Uroteuthis duvaucelii, also known as the Indian Ocean Squid or Indian Squid, is an Indo-West Pacific species of squid with a wide range throughout the Indian Ocean

records.name: industrial hydrogenated soybean and cottonseed shortening
aliases: industrial hydrogenated soybean and cottonseed shortening

records.name: instant coffee
records.description: INSTANT COFFEE is a beverage derived from brewed coffee beans that enables people to quickly prepare hot coffee by adding hot water or milk to the powder or crystals and stirring

records.name: invert sugar
records.description: Invert sugar is a liquid sugar syrup produced by splitting sucrose into its component parts—glucose and fructose—through hydrolysis using heat, acid, or enzymes, a process discovered in the 19th century and now widely used in food manufacturing rather than home kitchens. It has a flavor sweeter than regular sugar (since fructose tastes sweeter than sucrose) with a smooth, syrupy texture, and it's prized in baking and confectionery for resisting crystallization, retaining moisture, and extending shelf life in products like candies, jams, and soft baked goods. Like other sugars, invert sugar provides purely empty calories with no meaningful vitamins, minerals, or fiber, offering energy without nutritional value.

records.name: iodised salt
records.description: IODISED SALT - is salt mixed with a minute amount of various salts of the element iodine.

records.name: Irish moss
records.description: Irish moss (Chondrus crispus), also called sea moss, is a red seaweed that grows along rocky Atlantic coastlines, especially around Ireland and the Caribbean. In food, it's valued mainly for the natural gelling and thickening properties it gets from carrageenan, a compound extracted from its cell walls. It has a mild, slightly salty or neutral taste on its own, so it's usually blended into other foods rather than eaten plain.

records.name: isomalto-oligosaccharide
records.description: Isomaltooligosaccharide (IMO) is a short-chain carbohydrate composed of glucose units linked in branched α-1,6 bonds, found in trace amounts in fermented foods like miso, soy sauce, and sake, and produced commercially through enzymatic conversion of starch, a technology pioneered and widely commercialized in Japan since the 1980s. It has a mild sweetness, roughly 40-60% as sweet as sucrose, with a clean flavor and syrupy texture similar to corn syrup, making it a popular sugar substitute in protein bars, baked goods, and "low-sugar" products. Marketed as a prebiotic fiber that partially resists digestion and supports gut bacteria, IMO provides fewer calories than sucrose, though recent research has questioned how much of it is truly fermented in the colon versus digested as regular glucose, making its fiber and metabolic benefits somewhat contested.

records.name: jalapeno pepper
records.description: Jalapeño peppers are probably the most familiar chili in American and Mexican cooking — a good middle-ground pepper for both flavor and heat. The taste is grassy, slightly sweet, and vegetal with a clean, building heat.

records.name: java plum
records.description: Java plum (Syzygium cumini) is a tropical evergreen tree in the myrtle family (Myrtaceae), making it more closely related to cloves and eucalyptus than to actual plums.

records.name: Jerusalem artichoke
records.description: JERUSALEM ARTICHOKE (Helianthus tuberosus), also called sunroot, sunchoke, earth apple, or topinambour, is a species of sunflower. The tubers are sometimes used as a substitute for potatoes: they have a similar consistency, and in their raw form have a similar texture, but a sweeter, nuttier flavor; raw and sliced thinly, they are fit for a salad.

records.name: juice
records.description: Juice is the liquid extracted from fruits or vegetables, produced by pressing, squeezing, or blending, with a history stretching back to ancient civilizations that fermented or drank fruit juices, though modern commercial juicing scaled up dramatically in the 20th century with pasteurization and packaging advances. It has a flavor that mirrors its source—sweet, tart, or a mix—with a smooth, liquid texture, sometimes with pulp retained for added body. Consumed as a beverage or used in cooking, baking, and cocktails, juice retains vitamins (especially vitamin C) and antioxidants from its source, though it typically lacks the fiber of whole fruit and can be concentrated in natural sugars, giving it a higher glycemic impact than eating the fruit whole.

records.name: jujube
records.description: Jujube (also called Chinese date or red date) is a small fruit from the Ziziphus jujuba tree, native to China but now grown throughout Asia, the Middle East, and parts of Europe and America. Fresh jujubes taste crisp and mildly sweet, similar to an apple.

records.name: julienne mix
records.description: A mix of julienne cut vegetables.

records.name: juniper
records.description: JUNIPERS are coniferous plants in the genus Juniperus of the cypress family Cupressaceae. Juniper berries are a spice used in a wide variety of culinary dishes and best known for the primary flavoring in gin. Juniper berry sauce is often a popular flavoring choice for quail, pheasant, veal, rabbit, venison and other game dishes.

records.name: juniper berry
records.description: A JUNIPER BERRY is the female seed cone produced by the various species of junipers. Juniper berries are used in northern European and particularly Scandinavian cuisine to "impart a sharp, clear flavor" to meat dishes. Besides Norwegian and Swedish dishes, juniper berries are also sometimes used in German, Austrian, Czech, Polish and Hungarian cuisine, often with roasts (such as German sauerbraten). Northern Italian cuisine, especially that of the South Tyrol, also incorporates juniper berries.

records.name: kamaboko
records.description: type of cured surimi, a processed seafood product common in Japanese cuisine

records.name: kanpyo
records.description: Kanpyo is a Japanese ingredient made from dried strips of gourd — specifically the flesh of the calabash or bottle gourd (a variety called yūgao, related to what's sometimes called "bottle gourd" or "calabash" in English). To make it, the gourd is peeled into long, thin ribbons, then sun-dried until they become firm, chewy strips. Before use, the dried strips are rehydrated and usually simmered in a mixture of soy sauce, sugar, and mirin (or dashi) until they turn a light brown color and take on a sweet-savory flavor.

records.name: Kanzuri
records.description: Japanese fermented chili paste manufactured in Niigata Prefecture

records.name: Katsuobushi
records.description: simmered, smoked and fermented skipjack tuna

records.name: kefir
records.description: Kefir or kephir is a fermented milk drink similar to a thin yogurt that is made from kefir grains, a specific type of mesophilic symbiotic culture. The drink originated in the Caucasus, Eastern Europe and Russia, where it is prepared by inoculating cow, goat, or sheep milk with kefir grains.

records.name: kelp
records.description: Kelp is a type of large brown seaweed that grows in cold, nutrient-rich coastal waters, and it's become a fairly common food ingredient, especially in East Asian cuisines. Kelp is notably rich in iodine, along with other minerals like calcium, magnesium, and iron. It's low in calories and contains some fiber. It has a natural savory, oceanic taste often described as umami. Kelp is a common term covering many species across several genera, all in the order Laminariales.

records.name: ketchup
records.description: KETCHUP is a sauce used as a condiment. Ketchup is a sweet and tangy sauce now typically made from tomatoes, sugar, and vinegar, with assorted seasonings and spices. The specific spices and flavors vary, but commonly include onions, allspice, coriander, cloves, cumin, garlic, and mustard; and sometimes include celery, cinnamon or ginger.

records.name: khorasan wheat
records.description: Kamut (a trademarked name for Khorasan wheat) is an ancient grain with roots in the Fertile Crescent, popularized in the U.S. after seeds were reportedly brought over from Egypt in the mid-20th century, though its "King Tut's tomb" origin story is more legend than fact. It has a rich, buttery, nutty flavor with a firm, chewy texture, and its grains are notably large—up to twice the size of modern wheat kernels—making it popular in pastas, breads, and cereals. Kamut contains gluten but is prized for its higher protein and mineral content compared to common wheat, offering good levels of selenium, zinc, magnesium, and antioxidants.

records.name: kirsch
records.description: A kirschwasser or kirsch is a clear, colorless fruit brandy traditionally made from double distillation of morello cherries, a dark-colored cultivar of the sour cherry.

records.name: kiwifruit
records.description: KIWIFRUIT (often abbreviated as KIWI), or Chinese gooseberry is the edible berry of several species of woody vines in the genus Actinidia.

records.name: Kodo millet
records.description: Varagu, known in English as kodo millet, is another of India's ancient minor millets, cultivated for over 3,000 years primarily in the drier, hilly regions of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh. It's one of the hardiest millets, thriving in poor soils with minimal water, and is often grown as a famine-reserve or marginal-land crop. The small, round, reddish-brown grains have an earthy, mildly nutty flavor similar to other millets. Traditionally cooked like rice, ground into flour for flatbreads, or used in porridges and idli/dosa batters, it's also popular in fasting foods and diabetic-friendly diets. Nutritionally, kodo millet is notably high in dietary fiber and polyphenol antioxidants, a good source of iron and B vitamins, naturally gluten-free, and has one of the lowest glycemic indices among cereals.

records.name: kombu
records.description: KOMBU (from Japanese: 昆布, translit. konbu) is edible kelp from mostly the family Laminariaceae and is widely eaten in East Asia. There are about eighteen edible species in Laminariaceae and most of them, but not all, are called kombu.

records.name: Konjac
records.description: Konjac is a common name of the East and Southeast Asian plant Amorphophallus konjac (syn. A. rivieri), which has an edible corm (bulbo-tuber).

records.name: Kosher salt
records.description: Kosher salt or kitchen salt[1] is edible salt with a larger grain size than typical table salt and without common additives such as iodine.

records.name: Lactase
records.description: LACTASE is essential to the complete digestion of whole milk; it breaks down lactose, a sugar which gives milk its sweetness. Lactase is an enzyme that some people are unable to produce in their small intestine.[5] Without it they can't break down the natural lactose in milk. Lactase produced commercially can be extracted both from yeasts such as Kluyveromyces fragilis and Kluyveromyces lactis and from molds, such as Aspergillus niger and Aspergillus oryzae.

records.name: lactic ferments
records.description: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are an order of gram-positive, low-GC, acid-tolerant, generally nonsporulating, nonrespiring, either rod-shaped (bacilli) or spherical (cocci) bacteria that share common metabolic and physiological characteristics.

records.name: Lactiplantibacillus
records.description: LACTIPLANTIBACILLUS is a genus of lactic acid bacteria

records.name: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
records.description: LACTIPLANTIBACILLUS PLANTARUM is a widespread member of the genus Lactiplantibacillus, commonly found in many fermented food products

records.name: Lactobacillus
records.description: LACTOBACILLUS is a genus of Gram-positive, facultative anaerobic or microaerophilic, rod-shaped, non-spore-forming bacteria. Lactobacillus is the most common probiotic found in food such as yogurt, and it is diverse in its application to maintain human well-being. Some Lactobacillus species are used as starter cultures in industry for controlled fermentation in the production of wine, yogurt, cheese, sauerkraut, pickles, beer, cider, kimchi, cocoa, kefir, and other fermented foods.

records.name: Lactobacillus acidophilus
records.description: LACTOBACILLUS ACIDOPHILUS is a species of gram positive bacteria in the genus Lactobacillus. L. acidophilus is a homofermentative, microaerophilic species, fermenting sugars into lactic acid. These strains are commercially used in many dairy products in the production of acidophilus-type yogurt.

records.name: Lactobacillus bulgaricus
records.description: LACTOBACILLUS DELBRUECKII SUBSP. BULGARICUS (until 2014 known as Lactobacillus bulgaricus) is the main bacteria used for the production of yogurt.

records.name: lactobacillus casei
records.description: LACTOBACILLUS CASEI is a species of genus Lactobacillus found in the human urinary tract and mouth. The most common application of L. casei is industrial, specifically for dairy production.

records.name: Lactobacillus Helveticus
records.description: LACTOBACILLUS HELVETICUS is a lactic-acid producing, rod-shaped bacterium of the genus Lactobacillus. It is most commonly used in the production of American Swiss cheese and Emmental cheese, but is also sometimes used in making other styles of cheese, such as Cheddar, Parmesan, Romano, provolone, and mozzarella.

records.name: Lactobacillus reuteri
records.description: LACTOBACILLUS REUTERI is a Gram-positive bacterium that naturally inhabits the gut of mammals and birds. Although L. reuteri occurs naturally in humans, it is not found in all individuals. Dietary supplementation can sustain high levels of it in those with deficiencies.

records.name: Lactobacillus rhamnosus
records.description: LACTOBACILLUS RHAMNOSUS sometimes is used in yogurt and dairy products such as fermented and unpasteurized milk and semi-hard cheese.

records.name: lamb
records.description: LAMB, hogget and mutton are the meat of domestic sheep (species Ovis aries) at different ages. The meat of a lamb is taken from the animal between one month and one year old, with a carcase (carcass in American English) weight of between 5.5 and 30 kg. This meat generally is more tender than that from older sheep and appears more often on tables in some Western countries.

records.name: Lancashire cheese
records.description: Lancashire is an English cow's-milk cheese from the county of Lancashire.

records.name: langres
records.description: Langres is a French cheese from the plateau of Langres in the region of Champagne-Ardenne.

records.name: lard
records.description: LARD is fat from a pig, in both its rendered and unrendered forms. Lard is one of the few edible oils with a relatively high smoke point, attributable to its high saturated fatty acids content. Pure lard is especially useful for cooking since it produces little smoke when heated and has a distinct flavor when combined with other foods.

records.name: lard and vegetable oil household shortening
aliases: lard and vegetable oil household shortening

records.name: lard and vegetable oil industrial shortening
aliases: lard and vegetable oil industrial shortening

records.name: lardon
records.description: A LARDON, also called lardoon or larding, is a small strip or cube of fatty bacon, or pork fat (usually subcutaneous fat) used in a wide variety of cuisines to flavor savory foods and salads.

records.name: lasagne
records.description: LASAGNE are a type of wide, flat pasta, possibly one of the oldest types of pasta.

records.name: laver
records.description: Laver is a type of edible seaweed — specifically a red algae from the genus Porphyra (and related species like Pyropia). It grows on rocks in intertidal zones along coastlines, particularly in the UK, Ireland, Japan, Korea, and other coastal regions. It has a savory, briny, slightly mineral taste — often described as umami-rich, similar to other seaweeds.

records.name: leafy tips cowpeas
records.description: Cowpea leafy tips (sometimes called cowpea leaves, or by local names like "kunde" in Swahili, "ewedu" relatives, or "bean leaves") are the young, tender shoot tips and leaves of the cowpea plant (Vigna unguiculata) — the same plant that produces black-eyed peas. While most people know cowpeas for their beans, the leaves are widely eaten as a leafy green vegetable in parts of Africa (especially West and East Africa), as well as in South and Southeast Asia. Slightly bitter, earthy, spinach-like flavor, a bit more robust than spinach.

records.name: Leccinum
records.description: LECCINUM is a genus of mushrooms from the Boletaceae family

records.name: legume
records.description: A LEGUME is a plant in the family Fabaceae (or Leguminosae), or the fruit or seed of such a plant (also called a pulse). Legumes are grown agriculturally, primarily for human consumption. Grain legumes include beans, lentils, lupins, peas, and peanuts.

records.name: lemon peel
records.description: The skin or outer layer of a lemon.

records.name: lemon zest
records.description: The outer skin of a citrus fruit, removed through a zester.

records.name: lentils
records.description: Originating in the Fertile Crescent over 8,000 years ago, lentils spread across the Mediterranean, Middle East, South Asia, and beyond, becoming a dietary cornerstone worldwide. Known as "dal" in South Asia, they come in many varieties—red, green, brown, black, yellow—each with subtly different flavor, from mild and sweet to earthy. Quick-cooking and hulling-friendly, lentils are simmered into soups, stews, curries, and purées across cuisines, from Indian dal tadka to French lentille du Puy salads and Middle Eastern mujadara. Nutritionally, they're a powerhouse of plant protein, fiber, iron, and folate, making them a global staple for sustainable, affordable nutrition.

records.name: light syrup
records.description: Light syrup is similar to Golden Syrup, but is made slightly differently and is a bit thinner.

records.name: lightly salted butter
records.description: BEURRE DEMI-SEL is a butter with a salt percentage between 0,5 % and 3 %

records.name: lima bean
records.description: Phaseolus lunatus, commonly known as the LIMA BEAN, butter bean, sieva bean, Double Bean or Madagascar bean, is a legume grown for its edible seeds or beans

records.name: lingcod
records.description: Lingcod is a type of fish popular on the West Coast of the US, it's not actually a cod. It's related to greenlings. Flavor and texture: Mild, slightly sweet white fish with a firm, flaky texture. Often compared to halibut or cod but a bit more delicate.

records.name: liqueur
records.description: A liqueur is an alcoholic drink flavored variously by fruits, herbs, spices, flowers, nuts or cream combined with distilled spirits.

records.name: liqueur wine
records.description: Fortified wine is a wine to which a distilled spirit, usually brandy, is added. Many different styles of fortified wine have been developed, including Port, Sherry, Madeira, Marsala, Commandaria wine, and the aromatised wine Vermouth.

records.name: liquid smoke
records.description: LIQUID SMOKE is a water-soluble yellow to red liquid used for flavoring. It is used as a substitute for cooking with wood smoke while retaining a similar flavor. It can be used to flavor any meat or vegetable. It is generally made by concentrating the smoke from wood, but can contain any number of food additives.

records.name: liquorice
records.description: LIQUORICE or licorice is the root of Glycyrrhiza glabra from which a sweet flavour can be extracted.

records.name: little millet
records.description: Samai, or little millet (Panicum sumatrense, syn. Panicum miliare), is one of India's oldest cultivated minor millets, traditionally grown in the rain-fed hills and plateaus of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha for over 5,000 years. Its small, round grains carry a mild, subtly nutty flavor and light, fluffy texture when cooked. Valued for its resilience in poor soil and low rainfall, it's traditionally used as a rice substitute—steamed, boiled into porridge (kanji), or ground into idli and dosa batters—and is popular during religious fasting periods. Nutritionally, samai is rich in dietary fiber, iron, and B vitamins, has a low glycemic index, and is naturally gluten-free, making it valued in diabetic-friendly and gluten-free diets.

records.name: livarot
records.description: Livarot is a French cheese of the Normandy region, originating in the commune of Livarot.

records.name: lobster
records.description: LOBSTERS comprise a family (Nephropidae, sometimes also Homaridae) of large marine crustaceans.

records.name: local tender maize
records.description: Native to Mesoamerica and introduced to India centuries ago, tender local maize (Zea mays) refers to indigenous Indian corn varieties harvested young, while the kernels are still soft and milky rather than fully mature and dried. It has a starchy, mildly sweet, earthy flavor—less sugary than sweet corn but with a satisfying bite. Widely enjoyed as street food, it's traditionally roasted over open coals and rubbed with lime, chili, and salt (bhutta), boiled as a snack, or grated into curries, soups, and flatbreads. Nutritionally, tender maize provides dietary fiber, complex carbohydrates, and moderate protein, along with B vitamins, magnesium, and antioxidants like lutein and zeaxanthin, making it a wholesome seasonal staple across India.

records.name: lotus seed
records.description: Lotus seeds are the edible seeds of the lotus plant (Nelumbo nucifera), an aquatic plant grown widely across Asia, particularly in China, India, and Southeast Asia. Fresh seeds have a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor and a crisp texture, often eaten raw or lightly cooked. Dried seeds are used in soups, congee, and herbal tonics

records.name: lowfat half and half cream
records.description: Fat-free half and half is a bit of a paradox from a US regulatory standpoint. Real "half and half" has a legal minimum milkfat content — the standards of identity for half-and-half fall under 21 CFR Part 131, and specifically §131.180 sets the minimum at 10.5% milkfat. So it's technically an imitation or substitute product.

records.name: lupin bean
records.description: Lupin or lupini beans are the yellow legume seeds of the genus Lupinus. They are traditionally eaten as a pickled snack food. The lupin is devoid of starch, which is very unusual for a species of edible bean. Lupin allergy may cause life-threatening anaphylaxis in sensitive individuals. Only "sweet" varieties of lupin are used for human food

records.name: lychee
records.description: LYCHEE is the sole member of the genus Litchi in the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.

records.name: maasdam
records.description: MAASDAM cheese is a Swiss-style Dutch cheese.

records.name: Maasdam-type firm cheese with around 27% fat
aliases: maasdam type firm cheese with around 27 fat

records.name: mackerel
records.description: Mackerel is an oily fish, popular in cuisines around the world for its rich flavor and nutritional value. It is a general name for several related species of fast-swimming, saltwater fish (like Atlantic mackerel, king mackerel, and Spanish mackerel). It has a distinctive striped or mottled pattern on its back and a firm, dark flesh. Taste and texture: Strong, savory, somewhat "fishy" flavor compared to milder white fish. The flesh is soft and flaky when cooked, with a high fat content that keeps it moist.

records.name: Madeira
records.description: MADEIRA is a fortified wine made on the Portuguese Madeira Islands, off the coast of Africa. Madeira is produced in a variety of styles ranging from dry wines which can be consumed on their own as an aperitif to sweet wines usually consumed with dessert.

records.name: mahi-mahi
records.description: Mahi-mahi is a species of fish, it's sometimes called "dolphinfish," but it's unrelated to dolphins. It's a large, colorful saltwater fish found in warm and temperate waters around the world, known for its firm, lean, mildly sweet white-to-pinkish flesh. Flavor and texture: Mild, slightly sweet flavor with a firm, meaty texture — often compared to swordfish or tuna, but lighter and less oily.

records.name: maida
records.description: Maida is a highly refined wheat flour, milled from Triticum aestivum after the bran and germ are removed, leaving mostly starchy endosperm — a process that became widespread in India with industrial roller-milling. It has a mild, slightly sweet, neutral taste, making it a versatile base that readily takes on other flavors. Maida is used for naan, bhatura, puri, pastries, cakes, biscuits, and samosa wrappers, prized for its soft, elastic texture. Nutritionally, it's calorie-dense (~348 kcal/100g) but low in fiber and micronutrients (iron, zinc, B-vitamins), with a high glycemic index compared to whole wheat flour.

records.name: maitake mushroom
records.description: Maitake mushrooms (Grifola frondosa) are a type of edible mushroom native to Japan, China, and North America, where they grow wild at the base of oak, maple, and elm trees. Earthy, rich, and savory, often described as woodsy with a slightly peppery note. They have a nice meaty texture when cooked, similar to other polypore mushrooms. Popular in Japanese and other Asian cuisines — sautéed, roasted, added to soups, stir-fries, or used in broths. Their frilly texture crisps up nicely when roasted or pan-fried.

records.name: malt
records.description: Malt is germinated cereal grains that have been dried in a process known as "malting".

records.name: malted wholemeal rye flakes and flour
aliases: malted wholemeal rye flakes and flour

records.name: maltose
records.description: MALTOSE, also known as maltobiose or malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined. Maltose is a component of malt, a substance which is obtained in the process of allowing grain to soften in water and germinate. It is also present in highly variable quantities in partially hydrolysed starch products like maltodextrin, corn syrup and acid-thinned starch. In humans, maltose is broken down by various maltase enzymes, providing two glucose molecules which can be further processed: either broken down to provide energy, or stored as glycogen. The lack of the sucrase-isomaltase enzyme in humans causes sucrose intolerance.

records.name: mamey sapote
records.description: Mamey sapote (Pouteria sapota) is a large tropical fruit native to Central America and southern Mexico, cultivated by the Maya and Aztecs long before Spanish colonization and still widely grown across Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean today. It has a sweet, rich flavor often compared to a blend of sweet potato, pumpkin, and almond with honey-like notes, and a smooth, creamy, custard-like flesh beneath a rough, brown, sandpaper-textured skin. Eaten fresh, blended into milkshakes and desserts (notably popular in Cuban and Mexican cuisine), mamey sapote is a good source of vitamin C, vitamin A, and fiber, along with notable amounts of potassium.

records.name: mammy apple
records.description: Mammee apple (Mammea americana) is a large tropical fruit native to the Caribbean and northern South America, historically cultivated by Indigenous peoples across the region long before European colonization and still popular in Caribbean and Central American cuisines today. It has a sweet, aromatic flavor often compared to a blend of apricot, mango, and raspberry, with a firm, slightly fibrous orange flesh beneath a thick, rough brown-yellow rind that must be discarded along with the bitter seeds. Eaten fresh, or used in jams, juices, and desserts, mammee apple is a good source of vitamin C, fiber, and carotenoids, though it remains a relatively niche fruit outside its native tropical regions.

records.name: Margarine
records.description: MARGARINE is a spread used for flavoring, baking, and cooking. Margarine is made mainly of refined vegetable oil and water.

records.name: marjoram
records.description: Marjoram (Origanum majorana) is a somewhat cold-sensitive perennial herb or undershrub with sweet pine and citrus flavors.

records.name: Maroilles
records.description: Maroilles is a cow's-milk cheese made in the regions of Picardy and Nord-Pas-de-Calais in northern France.

records.name: Marsala wine
records.description: MARSALA is a wine, dry or sweet, produced in the region surrounding the Italian city of Marsala in Sicily.

records.name: marzipan
records.description: MARZIPAN is a confection consisting primarily of sugar or honey and almond meal (ground almonds), sometimes augmented with almond oil or extract.

records.name: mascarpone
records.description: MASCARPONE is an Italian cream cheese coagulated by the addition of certain acidic substances such as lemon juice, vinegar, citric acid or acetic acid.

records.name: mate
records.description: Mate is a traditional South American caffeine-rich infused drink. It is prepared by steeping dried leaves of yerba mate in hot water and is served with a metal straw from a shared hollow calabash gourd

records.name: mayonnaise
records.description: MAYONNAISE, informally mayo, is a thick cold sauce or dressing usually used in sandwiches and composed salads or on chips. It is a stable emulsion of oil, egg yolk, and acid, either vinegar or lemon juice.

records.name: meat patty
records.description: A MEAT PATTY is a flattened, usually round, serving of ground meat.

records.name: meatball
records.description: A MEATBALL is ground meat rolled into a small ball, sometimes along with other ingredients, such as bread crumbs, minced onion, eggs, butter, and seasoning.

records.name: medium rye flour
records.description: Medium rye flour is milled from whole rye with some bran sifted out, a grain long grown across Northern and Eastern Europe for its hardiness in cool climates. It has an earthy, slightly tangy flavor and a denser character than wheat flour. It's prized for European-style breads, sourdoughs, and crackers, though its lower gluten content means it's often blended with wheat flour or given longer fermentation for a good rise. Nutritionally, it offers more fiber, B vitamins, and minerals than refined wheat flour, with a gentler effect on blood sugar.

records.name: medium-coarse salt from the Alps
aliases: medium coarse salt from the alps

records.name: melado
records.description: Melado is an unrefined liquid sugar syrup made from concentrated sugarcane juice, a traditional product especially common in Brazil and other Latin American countries where it's produced as a byproduct or lighter-processed cousin of molasses, retaining more of the cane's natural sweetness. It has a rich, deep caramel flavor with molasses-like notes but milder and less bitter than true molasses, and a thick, syrupy texture. Used in traditional desserts, sauces, and as a spread or sweetener in Brazilian and Latin American cooking, melado retains modest amounts of minerals like calcium, iron, and potassium from the cane juice, making it slightly more nutritious than fully refined sugar.

records.name: merguez
records.description: Merguez is a red, spicy mutton- or beef-based fresh sausage from Maghrebi cuisine.

records.name: meringue
records.description: Meringue is a type of dessert or candy, traditionally made from whipped egg whites and sugar.

records.name: microbial culture
records.description: A microbiological culture, or microbial culture, is a method of multiplying microbial organisms by letting them reproduce in predetermined culture medium under controlled laboratory conditions. All cultures in food are microbial cultures

records.name: microbial rennet
records.description: Some molds such as Rhizomucor miehei are able to produce proteolytic enzymes. Cheeses produced this way are suitable for vegetarians, provided no animal-based alimentation was used during the production.

records.name: milk
records.description: MILK - a white liquid nutrient-rich food produced by the mammary glands of mammals.

records.name: milk chocolate
records.description: MILK CHOCOLATE is solid chocolate made with milk added in the form of powdered milk, liquid milk, or condensed milk.

records.name: milkcap
records.description: LACTARIUS is a genus of mushroom-producing, ectomycorrhizal fungi, containing several edible species.

records.name: milkfish
records.description: Milkfish (Chanos chanos) is a mild-flavored, silvery fish that's a staple food in parts of Southeast Asia, especially the Philippines, Indonesia, and Taiwan. Texture and flavor: The flesh is soft, slightly fatty, and has a mild taste that takes on marinades and seasonings well. It's notoriously bony, with many small, fine bones running through the flesh. This has led to specialty products like "boneless milkfish," where the bones are removed before selling.

records.name: millet
records.description: Millet is an ancient cereal grain domesticated in East Asia and Africa thousands of years ago, historically a staple in China, India, and parts of Africa long before rice and wheat became dominant. It has a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor with a light, fluffy texture when cooked, and a firmer, chewier bite when toasted first. It's naturally gluten-free and used in porridges, pilafs, flatbreads, and baked goods, offering a solid source of magnesium, phosphorus, fiber, and plant protein, along with antioxidants.

records.name: mimolette
records.description: Mimolette is a cheese traditionally produced around the city of Lille, France.

records.name: miso
records.description: MISO is a traditional Japanese seasoning produced by fermenting soybeans with salt and kōji (the fungus Aspergillus oryzae) and sometimes rice, barley, seaweed or other ingredients.

records.name: mixture of palm oil and palm superolein
