records.name: mizuame
records.description: A clear, thick, sticky liquid, it is made by converting starch to sugars.

records.name: molasses
records.description: Molasses (American English) or black treacle (British English) is a viscous product resulting from refining sugarcane or sugar beets into sugar.

records.name: monkfish
records.description: "Anglerfish" is a broad term for an order of fish (Lophiiformes) known for using a fleshy growth on their head like a fishing lure to attract prey. The fish sold as "monkfish" in seafood markets typically refers to species in the genus Lophius — like the American anglerfish (Lophius americanus) or European anglerfish (Lophius piscatorius) — which live on the seafloor in relatively shallow coastal waters. Monkfish is prized in cooking mostly for its tail meat, which is the part typically sold and eaten. Texture and flavor: It has a firm, dense, meaty texture — often compared to lobster — with a mild, slightly sweet flavor. This has earned it the nickname "poor man's lobster."

records.name: Monterey Jack
records.description: MONTEREY JACK, sometimes shortened to Jack, is an American white, semi-hard cheese made using cow's milk. It is noted for its mild flavor and slight sweetness.

records.name: morbier
records.description: Morbier is an AOP semi-soft cows' milk cheese of France.

records.name: Mortierella alpina oil
records.description: Mortierella alpina oil is derived from a soil-dwelling filamentous fungus, first isolated and studied for its lipid content in various regions worldwide, including Japan, China, and Europe, where it is produced industrially through fermentation. The refined oil is essentially flavorless and odorless, making it unobtrusive when blended into other products. It is primarily used as an additive in infant formula, nutritional supplements, and functional foods across global markets, valued for standardized quality and non-animal, non-fish origin. Nutritionally, it is notable for its high concentration of arachidonic acid, an omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid also naturally present in human breast milk and various animal tissues.

records.name: moth bean
records.description: Moth beans (Vigna aconitifolia), also called mat beans or matki, originated in the Indian subcontinent, where they've been cultivated for centuries as a hardy, drought-resistant crop suited to arid regions. Small, olive-brown, and oblong, they carry an earthy, slightly nutty flavor with a firm bite once cooked. Across South Asia, they're prepared whole or sprouted—simmered into curries, stewed with spices, or featured in dishes like Maharashtra's misal; sprouted moth beans also appear in salads and street snacks. Globally, they're valued as a protein- and fiber-rich pulse, contributing iron, folate, and other minerals typical of legumes within diverse traditional cuisines.

records.name: mozzarella
records.description: Mozzarella is a traditionally southern Italian cheese made from Italian buffalo's milk by the pasta filata method.

records.name: Muenster cheese
records.description: American cheese.

records.name: mung bean
records.description: Green gram, whole (Vigna radiata), commonly known as mung bean or moong, originated in the Indian subcontinent and spread across Asia and beyond through centuries of trade and cultivation. Sold whole with its green skin intact, it has a mild, slightly sweet, earthy flavor and a firm texture that softens on cooking. It's used worldwide in soups, stews, curries, salads, and sprouts, and is especially popular in Asian cuisines from India to China and Southeast Asia. Nutritionally, it's rich in plant protein, dietary fiber, folate, potassium, and magnesium, making it a light, easily digestible legume valued globally for everyday and health-focused diets.

records.name: mung dal
records.description: Split mung bean

records.name: Munster
records.description: Munster, Munster-géromé, or Minschterkaas, is a strong-smelling soft cheese with a subtle taste, made mainly from milk first produced in the Vosges.

records.name: muscadet
records.description: MUSCADET is a French white wine.

records.name: mussel
records.description: Mussel is the common name used for members of several families of bivalve molluscs, from saltwater and freshwater habitats.

records.name: mustard
records.description: Powder or paste made from seeds of the mustard plant, and used as a condiment or a spice.

records.name: mustard cabbage
records.description: Mustard Cabbage (also called gai choy or Chinese mustard) is a leafy green vegetable common in Asian cuisine. Large, crinkled or smooth leaves, often with a pale green or yellowish color; can look somewhat like bok choy or napa cabbage. Distinctly pungent and slightly bitter, with a mustardy kick that mellows when cooked.

records.name: mustard greens
records.description: Mustard greens are the leafy tops of the mustard plant (Brassica juncea), and they're a true member of the mustard family — grown specifically for their peppery, pungent leaves rather than for seeds or oil (though the same plant family produces mustard seeds too). Mustard greens have a distinctly sharp, spicy, peppery bite — similar to the kick you get from horseradish, wasabi, or arugula, but more pronounced. Cooking mellows the heat somewhat, but they still have more punch than almost any other leafy green.

records.name: mustard seed
records.description: A small, round seed of the mustard plant.

records.name: mustard spinach
records.description: Mustard spinach, also known as komatsuna, is a leafy green vegetable that's actually part of the mustard/brassica family (Brassica rapa var. perviridis) rather than being related to true spinach. It's an East Asian vegetable, especially popular in Japanese cuisine (where it's called komatsuna), though it's also grown and eaten in China and other parts of Asia. The flavor is mild and slightly peppery.

records.name: mutton
records.description: mutton is the meat of domestic sheep (species Ovis aries). The meat of an adult sheep is mutton, a term only used for the meat, not the living animals. Meat from sheep features prominently in several cuisines of the Mediterranean.

records.name: nance
records.description: Nance is a small tropical fruit native to Central America, the Caribbean, and parts of South America. Small, round, yellow to orange berries, about 1–2 cm in diameter, growing in clusters. It has a very distinctive, pungent aroma and a flavor that's a unique mix of sweet, sour, and slightly cheesy or fermented.

records.name: naranjilla
records.description: Naranjilla is a tropical fruit native to South America, mainly grown in Ecuador, Colombia, and Peru. Small to medium round fruit, about the size of a golf ball with bright orange skin covered in fine, removable fuzz. The flavor is very distinctive — a unique mix of tart, citrusy, and tropical, often described as a cross between pineapple, lime, and rhubarb.

records.name: neufchâtel
records.description: Neufchâtel is a soft, slightly crumbly, mold-ripened cheese made in the Neufchâtel-en-Bray, French region of Normandy.

records.name: new zealand spinach
records.description: New Zealand spinach (Tetragonia tetragonioides) isn't a true spinach at all. it's eaten much the same way as regular spinach — the young leaves and shoot tips are harvested and used cooked (steamed, sautéed, boiled, or added to soups and stir-fries). It's usually not eaten raw in large quantities because of its oxalate content, and cooking also helps soften its slightly thicker, fuzzier texture.

records.name: nigari
records.description: Bittern is a bitter-tasting solution that remains after precipitation of halite (common salt) from brines and/or seawater. It is rich in magnesium chlorides, sulfates, bromides, iodides, and other chemicals present in the original waters.

records.name: nile perch
records.description: The Nile perch (Lates niloticus), also known as the African snook, Goliath perch, Giant lates or the Victoria perch, is a species of freshwater fish in family Latidae of order Perciformes. It is widespread throughout much of the Afrotropical realm.

records.name: noodle
records.description: NOODLES are unleavened dough which is stretched, extruded, or rolled flat and cut into one of a variety of shapes which usually include long, thin strips, or waves, helices, tubes, strings, or shells, or folded over, or cut into other shapes.

records.name: nopales
records.description: Nopales are the edible pads (paddles) of the prickly pear cactus (genus Opuntia), widely used in Mexican cuisine. Slightly tart and grassy, a bit like green beans or okra, with a similar mucilaginous (slightly slimy) texture when cooked, especially if simmered.

records.name: nori
records.description: Nori (海苔) is the Japanese name for edible seaweed (a "sea vegetable") species of the red algae genus Pyropia, including P. yezoensis and P. tenera.

records.name: nutmeg
records.description: NUTMEG is the seed or ground spice of several species of the genus Myristica.

records.name: nutritional yeast
records.description: Nutritional yeast is a deactivated form of Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast, typically grown on molasses and then heat-killed before being dried into flakes or powder, popularized in the mid-20th century as a health food, particularly within vegan and vegetarian communities. It has a distinctly savory, cheesy, nutty flavor with umami depth, making it a popular seasoning sprinkled over popcorn, pasta, and salads or blended into vegan cheese sauces. Unlike active baking yeast, it has no leavening power since it's deactivated, but it stands out nutritionally as a complete protein source rich in B vitamins—often fortified with B12—making it especially valued in plant-based diets for filling that typical nutritional gap.

records.name: oat
records.description: Oats are a cereal grain that originated in Western Asia or Europe, historically used as animal fodder before rising to prominence as a hearty breakfast staple, especially in Scotland and Northern Europe. They have a mild, creamy, subtly sweet flavor with a soft, chewy texture that varies by processing—from firm steel-cut to quick-cooking rolled or instant forms. Oats are naturally gluten-free (though often cross-contaminated during processing) and are notable for their beta-glucan fiber, which supports heart health, along with solid amounts of protein, manganese, and iron.

records.name: oat flakes
records.description: Rolled oats are whole oat groats that have been steamed and pressed flat with large rollers, a processing method developed in the late 1800s to shorten cooking time while keeping the grain mostly intact. They have a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor with a soft, chewy texture that holds its shape better than instant oats, making them the classic choice for traditional oatmeal, granola, and baking. Like other oats, they're naturally gluten-free (if uncontaminated) and rich in beta-glucan fiber for heart health, plus protein, manganese, and iron, though their nutrition is nearly identical to whole oats since minimal processing preserves the bran and germ.

records.name: ōhelo berry
records.description: ʻŌhelo is a small, native Hawaiian shrub in the cranberry family, commonly found at high elevations on the islands of Maui and Hawaiʻi. Ōhelo is related to the cranberry but much less tart — mildly sweet and mildly tart, with a texture similar to cranberries or blueberries.

records.name: oil
records.description: Cooking OIL is plant, animal, or synthetic fat used in frying, baking, and other types of cooking. It is also used in food preparation and flavouring not involving heat, such as salad dressings and bread dips, and in this sense might be more accurately termed edible oil.

records.name: oil and fat
records.description: Several edible vegetable and animal oils, and also fats, are used for various purposes in cooking and food preparation. In particular, many foods are fried in oil much hotter than boiling water. Oils are also used for flavoring and for modifying the texture of foods (e.g. Stir Fry). Cooking oils are derived either from animal fat, as butter, lard and other types, or plant oils from the olive, maize, sunflower and many other species.

records.name: Okara
records.description: Okara is the fibrous pulp byproduct left over from pressing soybeans to make soy milk or tofu, a traditional ingredient in Japanese, Chinese, and Korean cooking where it's long been used to avoid food waste, particularly in dishes like Japanese unohana. It has a mild, slightly nutty, bean-like flavor with a dry, crumbly, fibrous texture similar to coarse meal. Used in stir-fries, veggie burgers, baked goods, and as a flour substitute, okara is notably rich in dietary fiber and retains a good amount of plant protein and calcium, though it's lower in protein than the soy milk or tofu it's derived from.

records.name: oligofructose
records.description: Oligofructose is a type of fructan—a short-chain fructose oligosaccharide—found naturally in plants like chicory root, onions, and bananas, and produced commercially mainly through partial enzymatic hydrolysis of chicory inulin, a process developed in Europe where chicory-based fibers are widely used. It has a mild sweetness, roughly 30-50% as sweet as sucrose, with a clean flavor and no notable aroma, and is used in food products as a low-calorie sweetener, fat replacer, and texture enhancer. Unlike simple sugars, oligofructose acts as a soluble prebiotic fiber that resists digestion in the small intestine and ferments in the colon, feeding beneficial gut bacteria while providing fewer calories than sucrose and supporting digestive health.

records.name: olive oil
records.description: OLIVE OIL is a liquid fat obtained from olives (the fruit of Olea europaea).

records.name: omelette
records.description: In cuisine, an OMELETTE is a dish made from beaten eggs fried with butter or oil in a frying pan (without stirring as in scrambled egg). It is quite common for the omelette to be folded around a filling such as cheese, chives, vegetables, mushrooms, meat (often ham or bacon), or some combination of the above. Whole eggs or egg whites are beaten, sometimes with a small amount of milk, cream, or water.

records.name: orange juice
records.description: Orange juice is the liquid extract of the orange tree fruit, produced by squeezing oranges.

records.name: oyster mushroom
records.description: PLEUROTUS OSTREATUS, the oyster mushroom, is a common edible mushroom.

records.name: pale brown amaranth seed
records.description: Amaranth seed, pale brown (Amaranthus cruentus), known regionally as Rajagaro (Gujarati), Ramdana (Hindi), and Cavali biya (Marathi), among other local names. Unlike the deep black-seeded variety, this pale brown form has a milder, subtly sweet, nutty flavor. In Indian cuisine, it's commonly popped and used in fasting foods (vrat ka khana), ground into flour for flatbreads, or mixed with jaggery to make chikki-style sweets. Nutritionally, it's a good source of plant protein, dietary fiber, iron, and calcium, and is naturally gluten-free—making it a popular grain substitute during religious fasting periods across India.

records.name: palm fat
records.description: the solid state of the vegetable oil, obtained from the fruit of oil palms.

records.name: palm kernel oil
records.description: PALM KERNEL OIL is an edible plant oil derived from the kernel of the oil palm Elaeis guineensis. It should not be confused with the other two edible oils derived from palm fruits:palm oil, extracted from the pulp of the oil palm fruit, and coconut oil, extracted from the kernel of the coconut.

records.name: palm oil and fat
records.description: PALM OIL is an edible vegetable oil derived from the mesocarp (reddish pulp) of the fruit of the oil palms

records.name: paprika oleoresin
records.description: PAPRIKA OLEORESIN (also known as PAPRIKA EXTRACT and oleoresin paprika) is an oil-soluble extract from the fruits of Capsicum annuum or Capsicum frutescens, and is primarily used as a colouring and/or flavouring in food products.

records.name: paprika or bell pepper
records.description: “Paprika” can be either the dried powder or the fruit of a plant in some languages. Put it only here if that is the case, otherwise put the ingredient under en:bell pepper or en:paprika.

records.name: parsnip
records.description: The PARSNIP (Pastinaca sativa) is a root vegetable closely related to the carrot and parsley.

aliases: partially hydrogenated soybean and partially hydrogenated cottonseed household shortening

records.name: pasilla peppers
records.description: A Mexican chili. The fresh version of this pepper is actually called chilaca. Once dried, it becomes "pasilla" — long, slender, and dark brownish-black with a raisin-like, wrinkled texture. Rich, deep, and slightly fruity with notes of raisin, dried cherry, and mild chocolate/tobacco undertones — a favorite for building complex sauces.

records.name: pasteurized butter
records.description: PASTEURIZED BUTTER is butter created from pasteurized milk

records.name: pasteurized skimmed milk
records.description: Skimmed milk (British English) is made when all the cream is removed from whole milk. It tends to contain around 0.1% fat. Láit écrémé has a maximum of 0.5% fat.

records.name: Patagonian squid
records.description: Doryteuthis gahi, also known as the Patagonian squid and locally as calamar, is a small-sized squid belonging to the family Loliginidae.

records.name: patty
records.description: serving of chopped ingredients formed into a disc.

records.name: pea
records.description: Peas are a good example of how the same plant can fall into different categories depending on how it's harvested and used. Fresh peas (green peas, snap peas, snow peas) are harvested young and eaten fresh, in or out of the pod. they are classified as a vegetable, not a pulse. Dried peas are the same plant, but the peas are left to mature and dry on the vine before harvesting. This is what counts as a pulse.

records.name: peach
records.description: The peach (Prunus persica) is a deciduous tree native to the region of Northwest China. It bears edible juicy fruits with various characteristics, most called peaches and others (the glossy-skinned varieties), nectarines.

records.name: peanut oil
records.description: PEANUT OIL, also known as groundnut oil or arachis oil, is a mild-tasting vegetable oil derived from peanuts.

records.name: pear
records.description: The PEAR is any of several tree and shrub species of genus Pyrus, in the family Rosaceae. Note this refers to the tree and not the fruit

records.name: pearl barley
records.description: Pearled barley is barley that has had its outer hull and bran layer removed through a polishing (pearling) process. This distinguishes it from "hulled barley," which only has the inedible outer hull removed and keeps the bran intact. Lower in fiber than hulled barley (since the bran is polished away). Good source of manganese, selenium, and B vitamins like niacin. Mild, nutty flavor with a pleasantly chewy, slightly sticky texture when cooked — it releases starch similarly to arborio rice, which is why it works well in risotto-style preparations.

records.name: pearl millet
records.description: Bajra is one of India's oldest cultivated cereal grains, especially prominent in the arid and semi-arid regions of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, and Maharashtra, where it thrives in low-rainfall, sandy soil conditions. The small, round grains range from pale yellow to grey, with an earthy, slightly nutty flavor. Bajra is traditionally ground into flour for rotis (bajra ki roti) and khichdi, or used whole in porridges, especially during winter months for its warming properties. Nutritionally, it's rich in fiber, iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, offers a good plant-protein source, and is naturally gluten-free—making it a staple in both everyday rural diets and gluten-free food formulations.

records.name: pepeao
records.description: Fresh pepeiao has a convex shape with a smooth, sometimes wrinkly surface, and can be a purply gray-brown color. It has a slightly chewy texture that many describe as rubbery-crunchy. It grows wild on logs of koa and kukui trees in Hawaii, typically on fallen or dying tree branches, often appearing after rain. It's known for its ability to absorb flavors when cooked and is commonly added to soups and stir-fries. It's a staple in Hawaii's Asian-influenced cuisine and is essentially the same category of mushroom used as "wood ear" or "cloud ear" in Chinese and Japanese cooking (sometimes called kikurage).

records.name: pepeiao
records.description: "Pepeao" is a Hawaiian word — it literally means "ear," and it's used in Hawaii to refer to a type of jelly fungus (wood ear mushroom, genus Auricularia) because of its ear-shaped, rubbery cap. It grows on dead or decaying wood and is edible, often used in soups and stir-fries, similar to how "wood ear" or "cloud ear" mushrooms are used in Chinese cuisine.

records.name: pepper
records.description: Peppercorns and the ground pepper derived from them may be described simply as pepper, or more precisely as black pepper (cooked and dried unripe fruit), green pepper (dried unripe fruit), and white pepper (ripe fruit seeds).

records.name: pepperoni
records.description: PEPPERONI is an American variety of salami, made from a cured mixture of pork and beef seasoned with paprika or other chili pepper.

records.name: Peruvian scallop
records.description: Argopecten purpuratus, common names the Peruvian scallop, is an edible species of saltwater clam, a scallop.

records.name: pesto
records.description: PESTO is a sauce originating in Genoa, Italy. It traditionally consists of crushed garlic, European pine nuts, coarse salt, basil leaves, hard cheese, all blended with olive oil.

records.name: Petit-Beurre
records.description: The "PETIT BEURRE", or "Véritable Petit Beurre", also known under the initials "VPB", is a kind of shortbread from Nantes, that is best known in France. It is the Petit Beurre of the LU society, which has become a success worldwide.

records.name: Picodon
records.description: Picodon is a goats-milk cheese made in the region around the Rhône in southern France.

records.name: pigeon pea
records.description: Pigeon peas (Cajanus cajan) differ quite a bit depending on whether they're picked green or left to dry on the plant. The green peas have a mild, slightly sweet flavor; the dried peas have Earthier, nuttier flavor — closer to lentils or other dried pulses

records.name: pilinut
records.description: A pili nut (Canarium ovatum) is a tropical tree nut native to the Philippines, particularly grown in the Bicol region. The nut has a rich, buttery flavor and texture, often compared to a cross between an almond and a macadamia nut — but generally considered even richer and more delicate. They're eaten raw, roasted, or candied, and are also used in pastries, pesto-style sauces, and as a snack food. In the Philippines they're a popular treat, especially when sugar-coated.

records.name: pink peppercorn
records.description: A PINK PEPPERCORN is a dried berry of the shrub Schinus molle, commonly known as the Peruvian peppertree. Although a peppercorn is the dried fruit of a plant from the genus Piper, pink peppercorns came to be called such because they resemble peppercorns, and because they, too, have a peppery flavour. As they are members of the cashew family, they may cause allergic reactions including anaphylaxis for persons with a tree nut allergy.

records.name: pita
records.description: PITA or pitta (British English), is a family of yeast-leavened round flatbreads baked from wheat flour, common in the Mediterranean, Middle East, and neighboring areas.

records.name: pitanga
records.description: Pitanga is a tropical fruit native to South America. The fruit is a berry with a persistent calyx up to 4 cm in diameter and eight clearly visible ribs. Its color changes from green to orange and purple as it matures. The flavor is unique — peppery and fruity, and quite complex

records.name: plain goat's milk yogurt with around 5% fat
aliases: plain goats milk yogurt with around 5 fat

records.name: pointed cabbage
records.description: POINTED CABBAGE, also known as cone, sweetheart, hispi or sugarloaf cabbage is a form of cabbage (Brassica oleracea) with a tapering shape and large delicate leaves varying in colour from yellowish to blue-green. It tastes less pronounced and more delicate than common white cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata f. alba).

records.name: pokeberry shoots
records.description: Pokeberry (pokeweed, Phytolacca americana) shoots are a traditional Southern U.S. food, often called "poke sallet" or "poke salad." The plant is toxic, but very young shoots can be made edible through careful preparation.

records.name: pomace brandy
records.description: Pomace brandy is a liquor distilled from pomace that is left over from winemaking, after the grapes are pressed.

records.name: pomegranate juice from concentrate
aliases: pomegranate juice from natural concentrated pomegranate juice

records.name: pont l'evêque
records.description: Pont-l'Évêque is an uncooked, unpressed cow's-milk cheese, originally manufactured in the area around the commune of Pont-l'Évêque, in the Calvados département of Normandy.

records.name: poppyseed
records.description: The seed of the poppy.

records.name: pork belly
records.description: Pork belly is a boneless and fatty cut of meat from the belly of a pig.

records.name: pork fillet
records.description: Pork tenderloin, also called pork fillet, pork steak[1] or Gentleman's Cut, is a long thin cut of pork.

records.name: pork loin
records.description: Pork loin is a cut of meat from a pig, created from the tissue along the dorsal side of the rib cage.

records.name: pork rind
records.description: Pork rind is the culinary term for the skin of a pig.

records.name: port
records.description: PORT wine (also known as vinho do Porto, Porto, and usually simply port) is a Portuguese fortified wine produced with distilled grape spirits exclusively in the Douro Valley in the northern provinces of Portugal.

records.name: portobello
records.description: Agaricus bisporus is a single species that's sold under several names depending on maturity and color strain: white button mushrooms (young, white variety), crimini/baby bella (young, brown variety), and portobello (mature, brown variety, large cap). So "white mushrooms" specifically denotes the white cultivar picked at an early stage.

records.name: pošip
records.description: Pošip is an autochthonous white wine grape that is primarily grown in the Dalmatian region of Croatia on the island of Korčula, although small amounts are also being grown on the Pelješac Peninsula.

records.name: pot barley
records.description: Pot barley is barley that has been processed to remove its fibrous outer hull but has not been polished.

records.name: potato
records.description: The POTATO is a starchy, tuberous crop from the perennial nightshade Solanum tuberosum.

records.name: potato starch
records.description: Potato starch is starch extracted from potatoes.

records.name: potherb
records.description: The young, tender leaves of genus Corchorus (mainly Corchorus olitorius and Corchorus capsularis) are cooked and eaten as a green vegetable, similar to spinach or amaranth greens. When cooked, the leaves release a mucilaginous (slightly slimy) texture, somewhat like okra — this is prized in many cuisines for thickening soups and stews.

records.name: poulsard
records.description: Poulsard (also Ploussard) is a red French wine grape variety from the Jura wine region.

records.name: poultry
records.description: Poultry are domesticated birds kept by humans for their eggs, their meat or their feathers.

records.name: pouting
records.description: Trisopterus luscus (bib, pout whiting, pout or most commonly pouting) is a seafish belonging to the cod family (Gadidae).

records.name: precooked parboiled whole grain brown rice
aliases: precooked parboiled whole grain brown rice

records.name: prickly pear
records.description: Fruit from plants in the Opuntia (or prickly pear cactus) genus.

records.name: protein
records.description: Protein is a macronutrient made of amino acid chains, sourced from a wide range of foods—animal sources like meat, fish, eggs, and dairy, and plant sources like legumes, grains, nuts, and soy—with humans relying on food-derived protein since prehistoric times as one of the three core macronutrients alongside fats and carbohydrates. Its flavor and texture vary enormously by source, from the rich, savory taste of meats to the neutral, often bland profile of isolated protein powders, which are typically processed from whey, soy, or pea into fine, mixable forms. Essential for building and repairing muscle, enzymes, and hormones, protein is measured by its amino acid completeness—animal proteins and a few plant sources like quinoa and soy are "complete," containing all nine essential amino acids, while most other plant proteins must be combined to achieve the same profile.

records.name: provolone
records.description: PROVOLONE is an Italian cheese. It is an aged pasta filata (stretched-curd) cheese originating in Casilli near Vesuvius.

records.name: prune
records.description: A prune is a dried plum of any cultivar, mostly Prunus domestica or European Plum.

records.name: psyllium
records.description: Psyllium, or ispaghula, is the common name used for several members of the plant genus Plantago whose seeds are used commercially for the production of mucilage. It can be used for the fibres or as infusion.

records.name: pulse
records.description: pulse = just the dry, harvested seed of specific legume crops. The UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) recognizes 11 categories of pulses: Dry beans — includes kidney beans, navy beans, pinto beans, black beans, lima beans, mung beans, adzuki beans; Dry broad beans — fava beans, horse beans, broad beans (in dried form); Dry peas — includes split peas, whole dried peas (green or yellow); Chickpeas — also called garbanzo beans; Dry cowpeas — black-eyed peas, blackeye beans; Pigeon peas — also called Congo beans or gandules; Lentils — includes red, green, brown, black (beluga), French (Puy); Bambara beans — also called Bambara groundnuts (earth peas); Vetches — common vetch; Lupins — lupin beans (also called lupini beans); Minor pulses — a catch-all for less common ones, such as lablab, jack beans, winged beans, yam beans

records.name: pumpkin
records.description: A PUMPKIN is a cultivar of a squash plant, most commonly of Cucurbita pepo, that is round, with smooth, slightly ribbed skin, and deep yellow to orange coloration.

records.name: purple coneflower
records.description: Native to the prairies and open woodlands of central and eastern North America, purple coneflower has long been used by Indigenous peoples before spreading globally as a cultivated herb. Today it's grown commercially across North America, Europe, and parts of Asia, with roots, leaves, and flowers harvested, dried, and processed into powders, extracts, teas, or tinctures. Its flavor is earthy, slightly bitter, and mildly tingling on the tongue. It's used in herbal teas, tinctures, capsules, and functional foods/beverages worldwide. Nutritionally, it contains polysaccharides, flavonoids, alkylamides, and trace vitamins and minerals, though it's consumed in small quantities as a flavoring or functional additive rather than a significant caloric or macronutrient source.

records.name: Quark
records.description: QUARK is a type of fresh dairy product made by warming soured milk until the desired amount of curdling is met, and then straining it.

records.name: quenelle
records.description: A quenelle is a mixture of creamed fish or meat, sometimes combined with breadcrumbs, with a light egg binding, formed into an egg-like shape, and then cooked.

records.name: quince
records.description: The QUINCE (Cydonia oblonga) is the sole member of the genus Cydonia in the family Rosaceae (which also contains apples and pears, among other fruits).

records.name: quinoa
records.description: Quinoa is an ancient pseudocereal native to the Andean region of South America, cultivated by the Incas for thousands of years and revered as a sacred "mother grain." It has a light, slightly nutty and earthy flavor with a delicate crunch, and its grains form a small, curled tail when cooked that gives it a distinctive texture. Naturally gluten-free, quinoa is notable for being a complete protein containing all nine essential amino acids, and it's also a good source of fiber, iron, magnesium, and manganese.

records.name: Quorn mushroom product
records.description: QUORN is a meat substitute product originating in the UK and sold primarily in Europe, but also available in 19 countries.

records.name: rabbit
records.description: RABBITS are small mammals in the family Leporidae of the order Lagomorpha. In some areas, wild rabbits and hares are hunted for their meat, a lean source of high quality protein. Domesticated descendants of the European rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus) that are bred and kept as livestock account for the estimated 200 million tons of rabbit meat produced annually.

records.name: Raclette
records.description: RACLETTE is a semi-hard cow's milk cheese.

records.name: radicchio
records.description: RADICCHIO is a perennial cultivated form of leaf chicory (Cichorium intybus, Asteraceae) sometimes known as Italian chicory because of its common use in Italian cuisine.

records.name: rainbow trout
records.description: The rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) is a trout and species of salmonid native to cold-water tributaries of the Pacific Ocean in Asia and North America.

records.name: raisin
records.description: A RAISIN is a dried grape.

records.name: raising agent
records.description: Raising agents are substances added to baked goods to produce carbon dioxide gas and create rise and lightness, with early forms like yeast used since ancient Egyptian times, while chemical versions such as baking soda and baking powder were developed in the 19th century as faster, more reliable alternatives. They are essentially flavorless or very mildly bitter/metallic on their own, though excess use can leave a soapy or tinny aftertaste, and they work by releasing gas bubbles that get trapped in dough or batter, creating a light, airy texture. Used across breads, cakes, and pastries—commonly as baking soda, baking powder, yeast, or ammonium bicarbonate—raising agents are used in such small quantities that they contribute negligible calories or nutrients, functioning purely as a leavening tool rather than a nutritional ingredient.

records.name: rapeseed oil
records.description: Rapeseed (Brassica napus), also known as rape, or oilseed rape, is a bright-yellow flowering member of the family Brassicaceae, cultivated mainly for its oil-rich seed, which naturally contains appreciable amounts of erucic acid. Rapeseed is the third-largest source of vegetable oil and the second-largest source of protein meal in the world.

raw canadian sea scallop without coral

records.name: raw emu oyster
records.description: The Emu Oyster is an egg-shaped fillet found along the backbone just above the thigh, with a thick sinew layer running through the middle. It's typically sliced thin for stir-fries or cooked low and slow until tender.

records.name: raw guinea hen meat and skin
aliases: raw guinea hen meat and skin

aliases: raw minced beef steak with 10 fat

aliases: raw minced beef steak with 15 fat

records.name: reblochon
records.description: Reblochon is a soft washed-rind and smear-ripened French cheese made in the Alpine region of Savoy from raw cow's milk.

records.name: reconstituted butter
records.description: RECONSTITUTED BUTTER - When combined with the correct ratio of water to restore a normal water / butterfat balance for butter, Concentrated Butter is called “reconstituted butter.”

records.name: red and green spined amaranth leaves
aliases: red and green spined amaranth leaves

records.name: red bean
records.description: Red Rajmah (red kidney beans) originates from the Andean region of Central and South America, from where it spread worldwide and became deeply rooted in South Asian cuisine, especially in Punjabi and North Indian cooking. It has a glossy deep-red skin with a soft, creamy interior and a rich, slightly sweet, earthy flavor. Most famously simmered into the classic "rajma" curry with tomatoes, onions, and spices, it's also used in soups, stews, salads, and rice dishes across many cultures. Nutritionally, it provides plant-based protein, dietary fiber, complex carbohydrates, iron, potassium, and folate, making it a globally cherished legume.

records.name: red kuri squash
records.description: Red kuri squash (often spelled 'kari') (katakana:ウチキクリ) is thin skinned orange colored winter squash, that has the appearance of a small pumpkin without the ridges.

records.name: red leicester
records.description: Red Leicester (also known simply as Leicester or Leicestershire cheese) is an English cheese, made in a similar manner to Cheddar cheese.

records.name: red palm fruit oil
records.description: Red palm oil is less refined than bleached palm oil

records.name: red plum
records.description: Plums with red pulp.

records.name: red rice
records.description: Red rice is a whole-grain rice variety that gets its reddish-brown hue from anthocyanin pigments in its bran layer, with well-known types grown in regions like Thailand, Bhutan, and the Camargue in France. It has a robust, earthy, slightly nutty flavor with a chewy, hearty texture, since the bran layer is left intact rather than polished away as with white rice. Naturally gluten-free, red rice is notably richer in fiber, antioxidants, and minerals like iron and magnesium than white rice, thanks to that retained bran layer.

records.name: red wine
records.description: RED WINE is a type of wine made from dark-colored (black) grape varieties. The actual color of the wine can range from intense violet, typical of young wines, through to brick red for mature wines and brown for older red wines. The juice from most purple grapes is greenish-white, the red color coming from anthocyan pigments present in the skin of the grape

records.name: reduced fat Maasdam-type firm cheese with around 14% fat
aliases: reduced fat maasdam type firm cheese with around 14 fat

records.name: refined olive oil
records.description: Refined olive oil is virgin oil refined using charcoal and other chemical and physical filters, methods which do not alter the glyceridic structure.

records.name: reindeer
records.description: "Reindeer" is used in Europe and Asia, and also refers to the domesticated populations found especially in places like Scandinavia and Russia. "Caribou" is the term used in North America (Canada, Alaska) for wild populations.

records.name: rennet
records.description: RENNET is a complex set of enzymes produced in the stomachs of ruminant mammals. Chymosin, its key component, is a protease enzyme that curdles the casein in milk.

records.name: rhubarb
records.description: RHUBARB is a cultivated plant in the genus Rheum in the family Polygonaceae. Rhubarb is stewed with sugar or used in pies and desserts, but it can also be put into savoury dishes or pickled. Rhubarb can be dehydrated and infused with fruit juice.

records.name: rice
records.description: Rice is a cereal grain domesticated independently in China and possibly India thousands of years ago, and it remains the staple food for over half the world's population, central to cuisines across Asia, Africa, and Latin America. It has a mild, subtly sweet flavor with a texture that varies widely by variety—from the fluffy separate grains of basmati to the sticky clumps of short-grain sushi rice. Naturally gluten-free, rice's nutrition depends heavily on processing: brown rice retains its bran and germ for fiber, B vitamins, magnesium, and manganese, while white rice is more refined and comparatively lower in nutrients.

records.name: Rice bean
records.description: Rice beans (Vigna umbellata) are a small, oval legume native to South and Southeast Asia, widely cultivated in northeast India, Nepal, Bhutan, southern China, Indonesia, and Thailand. They have a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor and a texture similar to mung beans, cooking relatively quickly compared to other pulses. Across their growing regions, rice beans are used in soups, stews, curries, salads, and fermented dishes, and are sometimes sprouted or ground into flour. Nutritionally, they are valued as a good source of plant protein (notably rich in lysine, methionine, and tryptophan), complex carbohydrates, dietary fiber, and minerals such as iron, zinc, and calcium.

records.name: Rice bran oil
records.description: RICE BRAN OIL is the oil extracted from the hard outer brown layer of rice called chaff (rice husk).

records.name: rice flour
records.description: Rice flour is a form of flour made from finely milled rice.

records.name: rice vinegar
records.description: RICE VINEGAR is a vinegar made from fermented rice

records.name: ricotta
records.description: RICOTTA is an Italian whey cheese made from sheep, cow, goat, or Italian water buffalo milk whey left over from the production of other cheeses.

records.name: roasted turkey including natural turkey juices
aliases: roasted turkey including natural turkey juices

records.name: root vegetable
records.description: ROOT VEGETABLES are underground plant parts eaten by humans as food.

records.name: roquefort
records.description: ROQUEFORT is a sheep milk cheese from the south of France. The cheese is white, tangy, crumbly and slightly moist, with distinctive veins of blue mold. EU law dictates that only those cheeses aged in the natural Combalou caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon may bear the name Roquefort, as it is a recognised geographical indication, or has a protected designation of origin.

records.name: rose apple
records.description: A rose apple (Syzygium jambos or related species) is a tropical fruit native to Southeast Asia and the Indian subcontinent. Despite its name, it's not related to either roses or apples — it belongs to the myrtle family. Pear- or bell-shaped fruit, usually pale yellow, white, pink, or red, with a waxy, smooth skin. Mildly sweet with a subtle floral aroma reminiscent of roses.

records.name: rosé wine
records.description: A ROSÉ is a type of wine that incorporates some of the color from the grape skins, but not enough to qualify it as a red wine.

records.name: rowal
records.description: Rowal (scientific name Pangium edule) is a tropical fruit native to Southeast Asia and the Pacific Islands. The fruits are generally 15–30 cm long, with a rough brown exterior. The flesh has a strong aroma. The fresh fruit and seeds contain hydrogen cyanide and are DEADLY POISONOUS if consumed without prior preparation.

records.name: Russell's snapper
records.description: Russell's snapper (Lutjanus russellii) is a species of marine ray-finned fish, a snapper belonging to the family Lutjanidae.

records.name: rye
records.description: Rye is a cereal grain native to Southwest Asia and Eastern Europe, historically thriving in cold, poor soils where wheat struggled, making it a staple grain across Northern and Eastern Europe and Scandinavia. It has a bold, earthy, slightly sour and tangy flavor with a dense, hearty texture, most familiar in dark rye bread, pumpernickel, and crispbreads. Rye contains gluten (though less than wheat) and is valued for its high fiber content, particularly soluble fiber that supports blood sugar control, along with good levels of manganese, phosphorus, and B vitamins.

records.name: rye grain
records.description: Rye grain hails from Central and Eastern Europe and Western Asia, favored for its hardiness in cold, poor soils. It has an earthy, slightly sour, tangy flavor with subtle spice notes. It's most often milled into flour for dense breads like pumpernickel, used for crispbreads, or malted for whiskey and beer. Nutritionally, it's high in fiber and B vitamins, with a lower glycemic impact than wheat.

records.name: sablefish
records.description: Sablefish is a deep-water fish found in the North Pacific, from the Bering Sea down to Baja California. Flavor and texture: Rich, buttery, almost melt-in-your-mouth texture, thanks to a very high fat content; Mild, slightly sweet flavor — less "fishy" than many other fish; Large, silky white flakes. Very high in omega-3 fatty acids, even more than salmon per serving

records.name: Saccharina japonica
records.description: Saccharina japonica is a marine species of the Phaeophyceae (brown algae) plant , a type of kelp or seaweed, that is extensively cultivated on ropes between the seas of Japan and Korea.[

records.name: safflower seed kernels
records.description: Safflower seed kernels are the inner, edible part of the seeds from the safflower plant (Carthamus tinctorius), an oilseed crop in the daisy/thistle family that's related to sunflowers. Safflower kernels are quite high in fat (mostly unsaturated, especially linoleic acid — an omega-6 fatty acid), along with protein and fiber. They're also a source of vitamin E and various minerals.

records.name: Sago
records.description: starch extracted from tropical palm stems

records.name: Saint Marcellin
records.description: Saint-Marcellin is a soft French cheese made from cow's milk, produced in the former Dauphiné province.

records.name: sapodilla
records.description: Sapodilla (Manilkara zapota) is a tropical fruit native to southern Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean. It's a small to medium-sized fruit with rough, brown, potato-like skin. The flesh inside is yellowish-brown, soft, and grainy in texture. Often described as one of the sweetest fruits in the world. It has a rich, caramel-like or brown sugar flavor, sometimes with hints of vanilla and pear.

records.name: savoy cabbage
records.description: Green cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) originated in the Mediterranean and Western Europe, cultivated from wild mustard plants over 2,000 years ago before spreading worldwide through trade and colonization. Today it's a staple across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas. Its tightly packed, pale-green leaves offer a crisp texture and mild, slightly peppery flavor that turns sweeter when cooked, with a subtle sulfurous note. Used raw in slaws and salads, fermented into sauerkraut and kimchi, or cooked in soups, stir-fries, stews, and stuffed dishes, it adapts to countless culinary traditions. Nutritionally, green cabbage provides vitamin C, vitamin K, fiber, and small amounts of various minerals, while being low in calories.

records.name: scallop
records.description: Scallop is a common name that is primarily applied to any one of numerous species of saltwater clams or marine bivalve mollusks in the taxonomic family Pectinidae, the scallops.

records.name: scup
records.description: Scup is a small saltwater fish found along the Atlantic coast of North America, from Nova Scotia down to Florida, though it's most abundant from Cape Cod to Cape Hatteras. Flavor and texture: Mild, slightly sweet white flesh, similar in character to other porgies or small snappers. It's a lean fish.

records.name: serrano peppers
records.description: Serrano peppers are a type of chili pepper originating from the mountainous regions of Puebla and Hidalgo in Mexico. They have a bright, crisp, and grassy with a clean heat — often described as sharper and more straightforward than jalapeño.

records.name: sesame oil
records.description: SESAME OIL is an edible vegetable oil derived from sesame seeds.

records.name: sesbania flower
records.description: The flowers come from Sesbania grandiflora, a fast-growing tropical tree also called the vegetable hummingbird, hummingbird tree, or agati. It's a popular edible flower across South and Southeast Asian cuisines. Before cooking, the bitter stamens and pistil inside each flower are usually pinched out, leaving the sweeter petals. They taste mildly sweet and slightly bitter, with a delicate, slightly crunchy texture once cooked.

records.name: shallot
records.description: The SHALLOT is a type of onion, specifically a botanical variety of the species Allium cepa.

records.name: shea butter
records.description: SHEA BUTTER is a fat extracted from the nut of the African shea tree (Vitellaria paradoxa). Shea butter is edible and is used in food preparation in some African countries. Occasionally, shea butter is mixed with other oils as a substitute for cocoa butter, although the taste is noticeably different.

records.name: sheep
records.description: Domestic sheep (Ovis aries) are quadrupedal, ruminant mammals typically kept as livestock.  Sheep are raised for fleeces, meat (lamb, hogget or mutton) , fat and milk.

records.name: sheep's-milk cheese
records.description: SHEEP MILK CHEESE is a cheese prepared from sheep milk.

records.name: sheeps milk
records.description: Sheep's milk (or ewes' milk) is the milk of domestic sheep.

records.name: sheepshead
records.description: Sheepshead is the common name for a few different fish species, most notably: (Archosargus probatocephalus), found along the Atlantic and Gulf coasts of North America. Taste and texture: Mild, sweet, and slightly nutty flavor; Firm, white, flaky flesh; Often compared to red snapper, black drum, or grouper; Because it eats mostly shellfish, crabs, and barnacles, some people say the diet gives it a faintly sweet, "crab-like" undertone

records.name: shellfish
records.description: Shellfish is a food source and fisheries term for exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates used as food, including various species of molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms.

records.name: sherry
records.description: SHERRY is a fortified wine made from white grapes that are grown near the city of Jerez de la Frontera in Andalusia, Spain. Sherry is produced in a variety of styles made primarily from the Palomino grape, ranging from light versions similar to white table wines, such as Manzanilla and fino, to darker and heavier versions that have been allowed to oxidise as they age in barrel, such as Amontillado and oloroso.

records.name: shiitake
records.description: The SHIITAKE (Lentinula edodes) is an edible mushroom native to East Asia, which is cultivated and consumed in many Asian countries.

records.name: Shorea robusta seed oil
records.description: SAL OIL (Shorea robusta seed oil) is an edible oil extracted from the seeds of Shorea robusta.

records.name: Sichuan pepper
records.description: Sichuan pepper is a spice made from the dried pericarp (outer shell of the fruit) of a plant of the genus Zanthoxylum in the family Rutaceae. (Wikipedia)

records.name: skimmed milk
records.description: LOW-FAT MILK is a 1% fat milk, sold in the United States. Skim milk (American English), is made when all the cream is removed from whole milk. It tends to contain around 0% fat.

records.name: skipjack tuna
records.description: The skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis) is a medium-sized perciform fish in the tuna family, Scombridae.

records.name: smetana
records.description: Smetana is a type of sour cream from Central and Eastern Europe. It is a dairy product produced by souring heavy cream. It is similar to crème fraîche (28% fat), but nowadays mainly sold with 9% to 36% milkfat content depending on the country. Its cooking properties are different from crème fraîche and the lighter sour creams sold in the US, which contain 12 to 16% butterfat. It is widely used in cooking and baking.

records.name: smoke
records.description: Smoke is a collection of airborne solid and liquid particulates and gases emitted when a material undergoes combustion or pyrolysis, together with the quantity of air that is entrained or otherwise mixed into the mass. Smoke is sometimes used as a flavoring agent, and preservative for various foodstuffs. Smoking is the process of flavoring, browning, cooking, or preserving food by exposing it to smoke from burning or smoldering material, most often wood. Meat, fish, and lapsang souchong tea are often smoked.

records.name: Smoked salt
records.description: SMOKED SALT is an aromatic salt smoked with any number of select bark free woods for up to 14 days.

records.name: snail
records.description: A snail is, in loose terms, a shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.

records.name: snow pea

records.name: sodium iodide

records.name: soft red winter wheat
records.description: Soft red winter wheat is grown primarily in the eastern and central United States, planted in fall and harvested in early summer to take advantage of its cold-hardiness. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor with a subtle reddish-brown hue in the whole grain. Its low protein and gluten content make it well-suited for cakes, pastries, crackers, and flatbreads rather than yeasted bread. Nutritionally, it's mainly a carbohydrate source, with modest protein and fiber, especially in its refined form.

records.name: soft wheat flour
records.description: Soft wheat has been cultivated for millennia, with whole-grain flour production expanding globally as milling techniques evolved to preserve the bran and germ. It has a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor that's less robust than hard wheat varieties. Its lower protein and gluten content make it ideal for tender baked goods like cakes, pastries, cookies, and flatbreads rather than yeasted bread. Nutritionally, it retains more fiber, B vitamins, and minerals than refined flour, thanks to the whole grain remaining intact.

records.name: soft white wheat
records.description: Soft white wheat is a low-protein variety grown mainly in the Pacific Northwest, California, and parts of the Midwest, prized for its adaptability to temperate climates. It has a mild, delicate, slightly sweet flavor with a pale color. Its low gluten content makes it ideal for tender baked goods like cakes, pastries, crackers, and flatbreads rather than yeasted bread. Nutritionally, it's primarily a source of carbohydrates, with modest protein and fiber content, especially when refined.

records.name: sorghum
records.description: Sorghum originated in Africa thousands of years ago and remains a staple across Africa, Asia, and increasingly the Americas, prized for its drought tolerance. It has a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor with a chewy texture similar to farro. It's ground into flour for gluten-free baking, popped like popcorn, brewed into beer, or cooked whole as a side grain or porridge. Nutritionally, it's rich in fiber, protein, and antioxidants, and being naturally gluten-free, it's a popular wheat alternative.

records.name: sour cream
records.description: SOUR CREAM is a dairy product obtained by fermenting regular cream with certain kinds of lactic acid bacteria. The bacterial culture, which is introduced either deliberately or naturally, sours and thickens the cream. Its name comes from the production of lactic acid by bacterial fermentation, which is called souring. Fat percentage is 18-20%.

records.name: sourdough
records.description: Sourdough is a naturally leavened bread made using a fermented starter of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria rather than commercial yeast, a method dating back thousands of years to ancient Egypt and still central to regional baking traditions like San Francisco's tangy loaves. It has a distinctive tangy, slightly sour flavor with a chewy, dense crumb and crisp, often blistered crust, shaped by the specific microbial culture of its starter, which can vary by region and even household. Made simply from flour, water, salt, and the starter culture, sourdough's slow fermentation is thought to improve digestibility and lower the glycemic impact compared to conventionally leavened bread, while offering fiber, B vitamins, and modest protein from the flour base.

records.name: soursop
records.description: Soursop is a tropical fruit from the Annona muricata tree, native to the Caribbean, Central America, and parts of South America and Africa. Large, green, spiky/prickly on the outside — it can weigh anywhere from 1 to 7 kg. The inside is white, creamy, and fibrous with large black seeds. It's taste is an unique blend of sweet and tangy — often described as a mix of strawberry, pineapple, and citrus, with a creamy texture somewhat like banana or coconut.

records.name: South African hake
records.description: Merluccius capensis (shallow-water Cape hake or South African hake) is a ray-finned fish in the genus Merluccius, found in the south-eastern Atlantic Ocean, along the coast of South Africa.

records.name: soy milk
records.description: SOY MILK or soymilk is a plant-based drink produced by soaking and grinding soybeans, boiling the mixture, and filtering out remaining particulates.

records.name: soy sauce
records.description: SOY SAUCE is a liquid condiment of Chinese origin, made from a fermented paste of soybeans, roasted grain, brine, and Aspergillus oryzae or Aspergillus sojae molds

records.name: soya
records.description: Soy comes from the soybean, a legume domesticated in China around 3,000-5,000 years ago and long a dietary staple across East Asia, later spreading globally as both a food crop and major agricultural commodity. It has a mild, earthy, slightly nutty flavor with a texture that varies enormously by form—from the firm bite of tofu and edamame to the smooth creaminess of soy milk and the meaty chew of tempeh. Extremely versatile, soy is used in countless forms including tofu, milk, sauce, and protein isolates, and stands out nutritionally as a complete plant protein containing all nine essential amino acids, along with fiber, iron, and isoflavones linked to potential health benefits.

records.name: soya bean
records.description: Soybeans (Glycine max) are a legume native to East Asia, cultivated for thousands of years and now grown extensively worldwide, including major production regions in the Americas, East Asia, and South Asia. Their flavor is mild and slightly nutty, adapting well to countless preparations. Soybeans are among the most versatile and widely used legumes globally, forming the basis of foods like tofu, soy milk, soy sauce, miso, tempeh, edamame, and soybean oil, as well as animal feed. Nutritionally, they are notable for their high plant protein content, along with dietary fiber, healthy fats, and various vitamins and minerals.

records.name: soya oil
records.description: SOYBEAN OIL is a vegetable oil extracted from the seeds of the soybean (Glycine max).

records.name: spanish peanut
records.description: Spanish peanuts are a specific variety of peanut, distinct from the more common runner or Virginia types you'd find as standard roasted peanuts or in most peanut butter. Grown mainly in Oklahoma and Texas in the US, though the name comes from their origin.

records.name: sparkling wine
records.description: SPARKLING WINE is a wine with significant levels of carbon dioxide in it, making it fizzy. Sparkling wine is usually either white or rosé, but there are examples of red sparkling wines.

records.name: speculoos
records.description: Speculaas or its variant speculoos is a type of spiced shortcrust biscuit.

records.name: spelt
records.description: Spelt is an ancient wheat variety that originated in the Near East and was widely cultivated across Europe, particularly Germany and Switzerland, from the Bronze Age until being largely displaced by modern wheat. It has a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor with a tender yet chewy texture, used much like wheat in bread, pasta, and baked goods, often prized for its more digestible protein structure. Spelt does contain gluten and offers a good source of fiber, protein, manganese, and B vitamins, along with more zinc and iron than common wheat.

records.name: spiny lobster
records.description: SPINY LOBSTERS, also known as langustas, langouste, or rock lobsters, are a family (Palinuridae) of about 60 species of achelate crustaceans

records.name: spirulina
records.description: Spirulina is a blue-green algae (cyanobacterium) that's grown and processed as a food and dietary supplement. Very high in protein (roughly 55–70% by dry weight), including all essential amino acids. Rich in B vitamins (especially B12-like compounds, though its B12 isn't well-absorbed by humans), iron, and antioxidants like phycocyanin (the pigment giving it its blue-green color). It contains omega-6 fatty acids (notably gamma-linolenic acid)

records.name: split pea
records.description: Split peas are dried, peeled, and halved seeds of Pisum sativum, a legume cultivated for millennia across Europe, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent. Available in yellow and green varieties, they have an earthy, slightly sweet, nutty flavor that deepens with cooking. Widely used worldwide — in Dutch erwtensoep, Indian dal, British pease pudding, Middle Eastern stews, and American split pea soup — they cook down to a soft, creamy texture without pre-soaking, unlike whole dried peas. Nutritionally, split peas are dense in protein, complex carbohydrates, dietary fiber, iron, potassium, and B vitamins, with negligible fat content.

records.name: spot
records.description: A small saltwater fish common along the U.S. Atlantic and Gulf coasts. Spot has mild, sweet, flaky white flesh. It's popular in Southern U.S. cooking — often pan-fried or deep-fried whole (scaled and gutted), since the bones are easy to work around once cooked. It's a favorite at fish fries in the Carolinas, Georgia, and along the Gulf Coast.

records.name: Stilton
records.description: Stilton is an English cheese, produced in two varieties: Blue, which has had Penicillium roqueforti added to generate a characteristic smell and taste, and White, which has not.

records.name: strawberry guavas
records.description: Strawberry guava (Psidium cattleianum) is a tropical fruit tree native to eastern Brazil. The flesh is white to creamy, with a sweet-tart taste reminiscent of a mix between strawberry and guava — hence the name. It contains small, hard seeds.

records.name: Streptococcus thermophilus
records.description: STREPTOCOCCUS THERMOPHILUS also known as Streptococcus salivarius subsp. thermophilus is a gram-positive bacterium, and a fermentative facultative anaerobe, of the viridans group. It is also classified as a lactic acid bacterium.

records.name: striped bass
records.description: The striped bass (Morone saxatilis), also called the Atlantic striped bass, striper, linesider, rock or rockfish, is an anadromous perciform fish of the family Moronidae found primarily along the Atlantic coast of North America.

records.name: sucrose
records.description: Sucrose is a disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose, occurring naturally in many plants but concentrated commercially from sugarcane and sugar beet—the two primary sources refined into the table sugar found worldwide. It has a pure, intensely sweet flavor with no notable aroma, forming the chemical basis for the many refined sugar products (granulated, powdered, brown, etc.) that vary mainly in processing rather than composition. Used universally as a sweetener in food and beverages, sucrose provides purely empty calories with no meaningful vitamins, minerals, or fiber, serving as a source of energy without nutritional value.

records.name: sugar
records.description: Sugar (sucrose) comes from sugarcane, first domesticated in New Guinea thousands of years ago and later spread through Asia and the Middle East to become the dominant global source, and from sugar beet, which took hold in Europe after Napoleon's early 1800s Continental Blockade cut off cane sugar imports and spurred domestic beet production, making it the region's primary source today. It has a pure, intensely sweet flavor with no notable aroma, available in forms ranging from fine granulated and powdered sugar to coarser raw and brown sugars with mild molasses notes. Used universally in baking, cooking, preserving, and sweetening beverages, sugar provides purely empty calories with no meaningful vitamins, minerals, or fiber, making it a source of energy without nutritional value.

records.name: sugar apple
records.description: A sugar apple (also called sweetsop) is a tropical fruit from the Annona squamosa tree, native to the tropical Americas and West Indies. It has a bumpy, knobby green skin made up of overlapping segments that look almost like scales or a pinecone. When ripe, the segments separate easily. The white, creamy flesh inside is sweet and custard-like — hence "sugar" apple. The taste is often described as a blend of vanilla, pear, and banana, with a grainy, melt-in-your-mouth texture.

records.name: sugar snap peas
records.description: Sugar snap peas — plumper, rounder pods (than mangetout) with full-size seeds, but the pod stays tender and edible

records.name: sultana
records.description: SULTANA is a "white" (pale green), oval seedless grape variety also called the sultanina, Thompson Seedless, Lady de Coverly, and oval-fruited Kishmish.

records.name: sundried tomatoes
records.description: Sun-dried tomatoes are ripe tomatoes that lose most of their water content after spending a majority of their drying time in the sun.

records.name: sunflower oil

records.name: sweet potato
records.description: A sweet potato is a starchy root vegetable. It grows underground as a swollen root, It's skin can be orange, purple, white, or reddish; flesh is often orange, but also comes in white or purple. It has a naturally sweet flavor, especially when roasted or baked. It is rich in beta-carotene (converts to vitamin A) and a good source of fiber, vitamin C, potassium, and manganese, and has complex carbohydrates, so it digests more slowly than many other starches

records.name: Sweet potato puree cooked with cream
